en: Oṃ, homage! Homage to Brahman!
[Now, the procedure for the barley-washing is written:]
May there be success in the commencement of the rite from this day forward. May there be success in the commencement of the rite from this day forward.
For the offering of water to the Sun.

Oṃ! To Viśvedevas and others, mother, father, maternal grandfather, and so forth; to the knower of the gods, the preceptor, and all—the increase of the water for the feet and the water for the guest-offering of the one seated here.
First, perform the placement [of the ritual items]. Self-worship. For the flower vessel: Oṃ saptavyādhā. Oṃ gayāyī namaḥ.
Oṃ gajādharāya namaḥ. Oṃ puṇḍarīkākṣāya namaḥ. Oṃ apavitrapa. Oṃ *sanno devī*. Oṃ kratave namaḥ. Oṃ dakṣāya namaḥ. To the Viśvedevas. Oṃ.
Gaurī, Padmā, Śacī, and Medhā; the world of the ancestors (pitṛloka); the astrologer, the preceptor (ācārya), flowers, and prosperity (vṛddhi).

Facing north, [place] the flower vessel. "From today onwards," "the performance of the sacrifice," and so forth. The invocation of the Viśvedevas: *Oṃ o māsaśca ṛṣmaṇo*. The invocation of the Pitṛs: "O fathers, from the fortnight... and so forth.
Oṃ, three steps. Oṃ, the wide realm of Viṣṇu.

Oṃ viṣṇornukaṃ. Oṃ tadviprāso. [Offer] water for the hands (*hastārghya*) together with *dūrvā* grass, *badarī* fruit, and so forth, to all the Viśvedevas and others. [Offer] sandalwood paste, the sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*), flowers, incense, and a lamp.

All [should perform] the formal resolve regarding the food (*anna-saṃkalpa*). In the case of the two mandalas, [one should recite] from *bhūḥ* up to the seven [worlds]. *Oṃ madhumatīr ṛtāyavaḥ*. From "today" (*adya*) onwards, [perform] the formal resolve regarding the food for the Viśvedevas and others. *Oṃ deva savitaḥ pra...*

Here, [offer] perfumes and so forth. Offer sixteen morsels of food (*gogrāsa*) to the group of Mothers (*mātṛgaṇa*). Perform the worship beginning with the seat (*āsana*), flowers (*puṣpa*), invocation (*āvāhana*), and so on. For all [deities], offer flowers for the *vṛddhi* rite. For all, offer the *arghya*. [Offer] sandalwood paste and so forth, the sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*), flowers, incense (*dhūpa*), lamps (*dīpa*), fruit, flowers, and betel leaf (*tāmbūla*).
May there be success for all! For the mandala: recite the hymn beginning with "vaṃcitāsi" and so forth for all.
Oṃ suprokṣitam astu namaḥ, etc. May all waters be auspicious. Oṃ, may Lakṣmī be present in the flowers;
Lakṣmī dwells in everything. To the Viśvedevas: may the offered food be pleasing. To the Pitṛs: [may it be so].
Food and water have been given; all food and water given to the gods, the wise ones, and others, reaches those for whom it is intended.
O you who are not terrible!

May the nine deities be satisfied. Facing the east, [one says]: "Of our lineage... Oṃ! May they increase our givers. May this very [offering] reach them. Svāhā! Let the speech be honored; let it be offered to the ancestors. This is the southern [direction]. Here, the offering of perfumes and so forth is made. Having performed the ritual with water for the sake of the right-hand [deities], then—
Having performed the Vedic worship, [there is] the limited fruit of the ritual. *Oṃ agnijyotiḥ*—the worship with the *Ṛgveda*.
*Oṃ tvaṃ javiṣṭha dā*—just as by means of the cause, the sacrificer attains the state of non-duality, so too through this [mantra].
Svānataṃnake | Dipaloharakṣā | Śagonanaṭvāye | Sarabhyadikāvāye ||

The tonsure ceremony (*cūḍākaraṇa*), the clipping of the top-knot (*śikhā-śaluna*), and the trimming of the finger-nails; the blessing with sandalwood and other virtuous substances; the consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*) with the *manojyotis* mantra; the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*); and the recitation for the avoidance of transgressions.
With "thaṃṭkādi" and so forth, [one protects] all people. Oṃ, may there be well-being for us from Indra.

The offering of sandalwood paste and other substances as a blessing; the consecration with the *manojyoti* mantra; the dismissal of the deities with the *gogrāsa* and other offerings; "Oṃ, may the gods come hither"; the concluding worship; and the offering of food to the assembly of sixteen Mothers and the fulfillment of the ritual for the ancestors.
Sephā Ārathi. Māsaghiḍi. For the sake of having the sun as witness. To Lāsāvathaṃtahe Duṃsalajānake.
Thus ends the ritual for the water of speed (javodaka-vidhi).
Oṃ, homage to Brahman; homage!
Now, regarding the rite of conception (*garbhādhāna*): when a woman has reached her menses, one should have her bathe on the fourteenth day thereafter.
The bride [attains] the sun, which does not fade; she becomes radiant, beautiful, and adorned with ornaments. She wears water and garments.

Having placed the *javodaka* (water for the feet) and other items, and having [prepared] the *kusaṇḍikā* rite with a person [acting as the priest], Brahmā performs the worship of the water-pot (*kalaśārccana*) according to the ritual procedure and with mantras, beginning with "Oṃ tat savitur vareṇyam" and so forth.
Door worship. Meditation.
[He saw] Brahmā, plump and yellow, with four arms, possessing four faces, riding upon a swan, and holding a staff, a rosary, and a water-pot.
Oṃ, homage to Brahmā.

Oṃ, salutation to Prajāpati. Oṃ, salutation to the Four-faced One. Oṃ, salutation to the one whose vehicle is the swan. Oṃ, Brahma, the first-born of knowledge. Oṃ, O Lord of Prayer (Brahmaṇaspati). Oṃ, may we partake of the Brahman. Oṃ, Agni who covers the dwelling.

The worship of the eight jars, beginning with the invocation (āvāhana): To Dharā: *Oṃ juṃ jatamana uta*. To Dhurā: *Oṃ idaṃ viṣṇuvi*. To Soma: *Oṃ irāvati dhenu*. To Aṣṭā: *Oṃ devaśrutau de*. To Anila: *Viṣṇorṇukaṃ vā*. To Anala: *Oṃ divo vā viṣṇu*. To Pratyuṣā: *Oṃ*.
Pratadviṣṇustavate | To Prabhāsa: Oṃ viṣṇorarāṭa.
This is the ritual procedure for the worship of Śagaṇa.
Oṃ *ākṛṣṇena* etc. || Oṃ *trātāram indra* || Oṃ *aśvastheya* etc. || The month and the lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*).
Balipūjā || Gaṇapati || Gogrāsa || Komālipūjā || Oṃ asmākam indra || Oṃ samita guṃ sa ||
Oṃ, Śrī is yours, Lakṣmī is yours. One should recite the four auspicious verses. Oṃ, you are the bearer.
Oṃ tejosi. Oṃ yāphalanī. Oṃ annapate. Oṃ manojyoti. [Recitation]. Praise.
Having established the meaning as the proof of the words.
The offering of clarified butter according to the procedure for the Caru sacrifice: "To Mārutāgni, svāhā!"—this is the oblation of ghee.

The oblation of sesame seeds (tilāhuti). The consecration of the ritual jar (kalaśapratiṣṭhā). The oblation for purification (saṃkṣāhuti). At the time of the bride’s departure, the tying of the auspicious knot (svastika), and the wearing of the wedding garment (poyakaṃkotāha). For the man to undergo the rite of shaving (nṛvaṃchanayāya). The dismissal of the ritual jar (kalaśaviśarjana). The bride is bathed with eight jars (aṣṭakalaśasnāna) accompanied by fruits and sprouts. Oṃ juṃ jana, etc. [The rite is] new.
In Luṃsipācaka, in Candramaṇḍalahlāya, and in Mevalaṃṣanamoḍahluyaka.

In the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), within the cloth of the intestines, the one who possesses the essence of the corners (the Sun) begs for the respectful offering (arghya): Oṃ! You who are being established, increase the embryo with milk; increase the image of the thousandfold, the one of universal form (viśvarūpa); touch the one who brings about destruction; make him long-lived. [The hymn] of praise.
One should recite the *Puruṣasūkta* for that person who is afflicted by the poison of a *koṇara* snake, while [the practitioner] sits upon a lion-throne in a dancing hall,
bowing down with joined palms at the feet of the Lord, according to the threefold truth.

Having performed the purification of the womb (garbha-śodhana) for the sake of crossing over the vessel of worship (arghapātra) with its head and feet [turned upward], one recites: "Oṃ, may he who is not overcome by the unassailable [power] bend down. Oṃ, may Pūṣan impel it; may Rudra fashion it as fatness;
may Tvaṣṭṛ eternally create forms for you; may Vaiśvānara bestow splendor."
Oṃ! He emits semen and enters the womb;
the organ is enveloped by the embryo and the fetal membrane, and he leaves the chorion at birth.
Oṃ! May Śinīvālī bestow a fetus; may Pṛthuṣṇukā bestow a fetus.
May the two divine Aśvins, born from the lotus, place a fetus within you.

Having first recited *metaṃ phaṃ*, [one should perform] the sprinkling with *siṃdhra laṃ uviya*. With *oṃ vasopavitra vidhitheṃ saṃpyāya siṃdharachāya*, [one offers] sandalwood and other virtuous substances as a blessing (*āśīrvāda*).
The touching of the heart: *Oṃ*! That which is your heart, O Soma, which is established in heaven within the moon—knowing that, may we know it;
may we see it for a hundred autumns, may we live for a hundred autumns, may we hear for a hundred autumns. [This is] the offering verse: *Oṃ*! You are the embryo of the plants, the embryo...
The embryo of the lords of the forest, the embryo of all that exists, O Agni, you are the embryo of the waters; Svāhā! The oblation is established. Om, the light of the mind.

Then, at the conclusion of the *lāsālāva* rite, having determined an auspicious moment (*śubhalagna*), one should perform the offering of the sacrificial porridge (*caruprāsana*) and recite the *svastivācana*.

Again, having sat down at the site of the sacrifice: worship of the Brahmins; the declaration of intent (*saṃkalpa*) for the *śāntika* food offering; "May heaven be peace"; the *puṣṭika* rite; the *tryambaka* mantra; the vessel filled with barley, grain, and parched rice; the *āsaṃsā*; the benediction (*āśīrvāda*); the dismissal of the fire (*agnivisarjana*); the consecration (*abhiṣeka*); the benediction (*āśīrvāda*).
The penis was brought forth; the maiden was revealed; for the sake of having the sun as witness; to the goddess Somaṇḍhā.
Thus ends the rite of conception (garbhādhāna).
Then one should perform the rite for obtaining a male child (puṃsavana).

On an auspicious day, having performed the sixth-month ritual, the bride’s bath, the *ovacona* ceremony, and the water-offering for the *thaṃka* and other deities, [the groom] proceeds with the prince [to the wedding site], accompanied by a red-colored canopy, banners, and so forth.
At the door, [offerings] for the Kumārapas, Laṃsoya, Thaṃka, and others; at the Mālako, for the Kiṃpikas;

at Luṃ, for the Garbha-āgāva-yosa-caka and the Brāhmaṇas; at Thāpara, for Yāṃvina, with red cloth and *sagvana*; at Ye, for Vina, the *bali*; at Hṅavana, for Balicchi; at Hṅavana, for Luḍu, and for Vāpini.

In the Ḍukelivana [ritual]: the offering to the Sun (sūryārgha), the placement of the Gāyatrī (gāyatrī-nyāsa), the worship of the arghya vessel (arghapātra-pūjā), and the self-worship (ātmapūjā). Oṃ tat savitur vareṇyam | Oṃ devasya tvā savituḥ prasave | Oṃ gaṇānāṃ tvā gaṇapatiṃ havāmahe |

Oṃ Bṛhaspate. Oṃ Catvārī śṛṅgā. Oṃ Dvāro devī. Oṃ Hiraṇyagarbha. Oṃ Sapta ṛṣayaḥ. Oṃ Brahma yajñānam. Oṃ Viṣṇorarāṭam. Oṃ Namaḥ saṃbhavāya. Oṃ Ājighra kalaśam. Oṃ Jatrapānāsam. Kumāla kalaśa. Oṃ Ākṛṣṇena ityādi. Oṃ.
*Trātāram indram*, etc. *Oṃ asvasthe vātya oṃ arddhamāsā*. *Oṃ agne pakṣati*.

Worship with *sāgonavastra* (garment of hemp): Oṃ dadhikrāṇo | Oṃ dīrghāyustvā | Oṃ tvaṃjaviṣṭhadā | Oṃ yāphalanā | Oṃ vasopavitra || Worship with the *bali* offering: Oṃ gaṇānāṃ tvā | [East] Oṃ jātavedase | [South] Oṃ imā rudrā | [West] Oṃ ghṛtaṃ ghṛtapāvāna | [North] Oṃ namaḥ ||
To the tawny one. In the middle. (****)(? || Oṃ, you who have eyes on all sides. An offering at the front. On the skin.
Oṃ, may you be long-lived. Oṃ, O Indra, [be] ours. Oṃ, Bṛhaspati, you are the roof. The umbrella. Oṃ, well-kindled... sa.
Hnasakana || Oṃ Śrīśvate Lakṣmī || Siṃdhara Muṇḍa || Catu Svasti || Oṃ Dhūrasi || Oṃ Tejosi || Oṃ Jāphalanī || Oṃ Annapate ||

Oṃ, the consecration of the mind-lamp. Recitation and hymn of praise. Here, the offering of fragrance and so forth. These are the offerings by the Brahmin; this is the Brahmin’s worship. To the Thaṅka and other objects, the Brahmin should recite the Svastivācana and other prayers.

At the *vadhulāsāla* [ceremony], the bride, seated upon an auspicious throne (*svastikāsana*) facing east, is adorned by the groom. Having performed the crossing over the *arghapātra* vessel, he performs the *svānataṃtanaka*. Then, having offered the *dyau-śāti* oblation, he pronounces the syllable *phaṃ*. After striking with the *tāḍacā*, he offers the red cloth along with the *sagona-nadvāya* and bestows blessings such as sandalwood paste and the like.
In the presence of a person.
For the worship of the Youthful Vase.
The worship of men, women, and their companions; the woman’s fodder and its placement; having first performed the water-offering (argha) to the sun.

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*), [perform] the worship of the *argha* vessel, the self-worship, [and the offering of] red sandalwood and so forth. *oṃ tatvājāmi* | *oṃ devasya tvā* | *oṃ gaṇānāṃ tvā* | *oṃ bṛhaspate* | *oṃ catvāri śṛṅgā* | *oṃ dvāro devī* | *oṃ asmākam indra* | *oṃ bṛhaspate chedir asi* | *oṃ ketukarṇaṃ na* | *oṃ*
The collarbone was present; then followed the worship.
Oṃ, salutations to the power of the foundation (Ādhāraśakti). Salutations to Ananta.
To the lotus posture; to the filaments and nectar; to the pericarp and the peacock seat.
Homage to Kumāra! Meditation:
One should contemplate the god Kumāra as seated upon a lotus, red in color, with two arms, and clad in red garments; he holds a spear in his hand and bestows boons.
Oṃ, homage to Skanda! Homage to him who has the form of a child! Homage to Vatuka! Homage to the one of red complexion!
Salutation to the one with a spear in hand; salutation to the one with a sword-like face.
Oṃ, you first cried out. Oṃ, O dark earth. Oṃ, Agni is the head.
Oṃ, with the Indras, Indra, the tawny one. Oṃ, may the Vasus and the Vasus be mine. Oṃ, may there be wealth for the one who possesses joints.

Oṃ, to Gajakarṇa, lord of the planets; in the east: Oṃ, to Kurkuṇa, lord of peacocks; in the south: Oṃ, to Ghaṇṭakarṇa, lord of the water-jars; in the west: Oṃ, to Lambodara, lord of the *sālmali* tree; in the north: Oṃ, to Kumāra, lord of peacocks; in the center: [to] Kekā, together with men and women. Oṃ.
O long-lived one, in the hair-tuft! Oṃ, the seed of the fruit! In the ketu accompanied by fruit! Oṃ, O herb, protect!
One should recite the Svastivācana. Red sandalwood. Oṃ jadayaka. Red sacred thread (yajñopavīta). Red flowers. Oṃ yatrapānā. Oṃ samita guṃ saṃ. Oṃ śrīścate lakṣmī. Oṃ asmākamiṃdra. Oṃ.

O Bṛhaspati, you are the splendor. One should recite the fourfold auspiciousness: *oṃ dhur asi*, *oṃ tejo 'si*, *oṃ japhalana*, *oṃ tavavāyuvṛha*. The food offering (*naivedya*) consists of molasses and rice. *Oṃ annapate 'nnam*. *Oṃ mano jūtiḥ*.
Consecration | Recitation | Hymn of Praise

Oṃ! May [the goddess] whose tongue is Gaṅgā, Kārttikeya, and Umā go forth to the lord of all the earth, the god of gods, Kumāra, who wanders through the expanse of the sky with a pure golden staff in his hand and for whom the peacock of fame [pursues him].
Salutations to that Kumāra and to Skanda, the wielder of the spear.
Obeisance to you, the youthful one in the form of fire, the lord of the planets.
"May he destroy my sins," etc. [Recite this]. The mandala. Water for sipping (ācamana). Offering sandalwood paste and flowers.
One should destroy the affliction caused by planets in their own houses. This is the ritual for Raktavidhi and the worship of the Kumāra-kalaśa.
To the one with the corner of a red garment; to the one with the white garment.
Then one should perform the Puṃsavana rite, [offering] many libations.

Taking *kuśa* grass and thorns, [he] leads them individually to the north for the purification rite (*śucilambhana*). At the edge of the cow-dung mandala, he leads the person to the north. He brings the medicinal herbs (*oṣadhī*) to the south. He brings the *kumārālaga* to the west. With many *siñca* flowers, he goes toward the southern direction; with *kuśa* grass, he goes toward the northern direction. [He places] the iron...

O you two, rejoice! This is for the sake of the desire for a son, not for the sake of worship. It is purified by the Gāyatrī mantra and by the Puruṣasūkta. [Offer] a southern packet. *Oṃ dhāmacchad agnir indro brahmā devo bṛhaspatiḥ | Sacetaso viśve devā yajñaṃ prāvantu naḥ śubhe ||* May Agni, Indra, Brahmā, the god Bṛhaspati, and all the Viśvedevas, being of one mind, protect our sacrifice for the sake of auspiciousness.

Uttarapoṭala, saḥ. Oṃ Brahmaṇaspate. One should contemplate the "loss of the seed" (bījahāni). At the conclusion of the sequence of the *velā*, one should recite the *svastivācana* for the person by means of a Brāhmaṇa. At the conclusion of the many *javanahāsa*s, [one recites] Oṃ Hiraṇyagarbha at the conclusion of the *avahnāsa-sakuśa*. Oṃ adya-saṃbhṛta-pṛ...
The protection of the mantra within the womb.
Oṃ, you are the fair-winged Garuḍa. Oṃ, may Indra grant us well-being and renown among men. Oṃ, the light of the mind; the firm foundation.
For the purpose of leaping over and maintaining [the state] in Thaṃkā and other locations.
The resolution regarding the food and the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) should be made by the Brāhmaṇas at the beginning of the rite for the Kumāra-ghaṇṭā.

Recitation: *svānataṃne*. Oṃ, to Sumuṣā. Oṃ, to the chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*). Oṃ, to the Lord of Planets (*grahādhipati*). Oṃ, to that Kumāra. Here [is offered] sandalwood paste and other items. Recitation for the purpose of overcoming transgressions; [offering of] men, women, and all things such as incense, sandalwood, and so forth; the bestowing of blessings (*āśīrvāda*); the *sephaṃ*; the *ārathi*; and the *ḍeke viye*.
Oṣadhīṣo-sacye-thaṃso-asyaṃ-maccha-naditaraṇa-krūrakarmma-kṣurakarmma-vivarjita-puruṣa-strī-kṛtakarmma-sākhine arghaṃ namaḥ. Thus ends the rite of *puṃsavana*.
Sūryaśaka, the Mālavīya.
Then one should perform the *sīmantonnayana* rite and the daily worship of the Kumārakalaśa; [this applies] to women who have not yet given birth.

For the offering of the moving water: [recite] *thaṃ* and so forth. For Nārāyaṇa, [recite] *ṇaṃ laṃ so ya*. For the door, the lamp, and the protection of the iron [enclosure], [recite] the benediction (*āśīrvāda*). For the deity in the *lāsāla* [shrine], [recite] *devatvaṃ*. For the vase (*kalaśa*), [recite] *yāvinaṃte*. For Gaṇapati and the others, the offering of the *bali* is performed.
Having offered the eighth [portion] with *yaṃvina*, the neck-cloth (*galavastra*) is presented along with the *goṇata*; this is the completion of the sacrificial rite (*saṃpyāyajusana*).

The state of Nārāyaṇa is attained through the fire-rite (agnikārya) performed with the personified vessel (puruṣakalaśa) in the treasury of the garland of planets; the worship of the jar (kalaśārccana) is performed according to the rules and with mantras.

To Brahmākala, the Brahman, in the form of Prajāpati: this seat, this flower, obeisance (*namaḥ*). *Oṃ tat tvā yāmi*, etc. [Recite]. Worship of the Door: to the Lotus Seat; to the Swan Seat; to Brahmā.
Meditative absorption.
Oṃ, [I meditate upon] Brahmā, who is yellowish-red, four-armed, and four-faced;
he is mounted upon a swan and holds a staff, a rosary, and a white water-pot.
To Brahmā, the embodiment of Prajāpati, the flower of meditation; obeisance! Obeisance to Brahmā! To Prajāpati!
To the four-faced one; to the one seated upon a swan; *Oṃ* Brahman, that primordial wisdom...; *Oṃ* O Lord of Prayer (*Brahmaṇaspati*)...;

*Oṃ* [to] the Brāhmaṇas also...; *Oṃ* Agni who covers the abodes...; to Dhara; *Oṃ* they yoke the mind...; to Dhura; *Oṃ* Viṣṇu pervades this...; to Soma; *Oṃ* the nourishing milch-cow...; salutation to the Waters (*Adbhyaḥ*); *Oṃ* O gods, hear ye...; to Devaśruta.
Salutation to Alila. Oṃ viṣṇoṇukaṃvī. Salutation to Anala. Oṃ divo vā viṣṇu. Salutation to Pratyuṣa.
Oṃ *pratadviṣṇustavate*. Homage to Prabhāsa! Oṃ *viṣṇorarāṭam*. Oṃ *ākṛṣṭa*, etc. Oṃ *trātāram indram*, etc.
The worship and ritual adoration of Keśava.
Oṃ, I approach the reality. Oṃ, by the impulse of the god. Salutation to the twelve forms beginning with Keśava. Oṃ, the wide realm of Viṣṇu.
Oṃ śrīścate lakṣmī. Oṃ pāvakānasarasvatī. Oṃ tvaṃ javiṣṭha dāśuṣe. [Perform] the invocation and other rites.

For the worship with the eight auspicious cloths (*aṣṭamaṅgalavastrapūjā*), I offer these [mantras] for the sake of fulfillment: *oṃ dadhikrāvṇo*; *oṃ tvaṃ javiṣṇudā*; *oṃ dīrghāyustvā*; *oṃ yā phalinī*; *oṃ vaso pavitra*;
*oṃ asvasti vetyādi*; *oṃ rakṣohanam*.
Again, the Brahmāsa-pūjā: Oṃ arddhamāsā | Oṃ nakṣatrebhyaḥ svāhā | Oṃ yoge yoge |
Balipūjā: Oṃ gaṇānāṃ tvā ga... | Oṃ jātavedase | Oṃ imā rudrāya |
Oṃ, ghee, O drinkers of ghee! Oṃ, salutations to Vabhrūsī! Oṃ, the unassailable!
Dukhāpiṃṣā || Oṃ, [offering] to the Goddess Samakṣā || Gaṇa || Cow-grazing fodder || Worship of Komārī || Oṃ, obeisance to the Gaṇas || Oṃ, to Āyaṅgava || Oṃ, to Jātavedas ||

Oṃ asmākam indra. Oṃ samit guṃ. Oṃ śrīśca te lakṣmīśca. One should recite the four *svasti* verses. Oṃ dhur asi. Oṃ tejo 'si. Oṃ yā phalinī. Oṃ annapate. Oṃ mano jyotiḥ. *Pratiṣṭhā*. The stream of recitation (*jāpa*).
Having performed the preparation of the sacrificial materials, [one performs] the preparation of the *caru* oblation.

Oṃ, you are grain. [One should place the rice. Oṃ, you are a cock. [Having performed the threshing. Oṃ, you are the increaser of the bull. [One should place the rice in a winnowing basket. Oṃ, blow away the husks! [One should remove the chaff and heads of grain. Oṃ, may the god [Indra] purify you. [One should place the rice inside the cooking pot. Oṃ, may the waters purify you. [The bestowing of nectar.]
[Pouring] from the vessel into the bowl: *Oṃ iṣatvorjja tvā*.
To the shoulder-body. He pours [the clarified butter] from the vessel of clarified butter: *oṃ agniṃ gaccha svayajamānāya bindu svāhā* (Oṃ, go to Agni;
for your own sacrificer, bindu svāhā); *oṃ viṣṇuṃ gaccha svayajamānāya bindu svāhā* (Oṃ, go to Viṣṇu; for your own sacrificer, bindu svāhā). This is the name of the fire-offering (*agniyā*).
Svāhā to Maṅgalāgni! Having offered an oblation of ghee, and having offered a full oblation of ghee followed by an oblation of sesame seeds.
Brahmā, having offered all the *tilāhuti* oblations at the site of the primary deity, performed the consecration of the water-pot (*kalaśa-pratiṣṭhā*).
The concluding oblation.

O Vadhulāsāla, on the Svastika seat, facing east: *oṃ rakṣohanam* [is for] the *mimyāla*. *oṃ adhyavocati* [is for] the *bali*. For the dismissal of the eight jars (*aṣṭakalasa-visarjana*): [it is performed] with the eight jars for the purpose of bathing. *oṃ juṃ jata*, etc., is for the *cyākaṇḍi*. Here, the crossing over (*laṅghana*) and the request for bathing are performed. Here.
The state of being clothed in rags.

At Lāsālā, on the auspicious eighth day of the waxing moon, [the ceremony was performed] with a vessel for the offering of water (arghapātra) and a ceremonial cloth (laṃṣana). The bride and groom, together with their attendants, were seated.
The protection of the fire-lamp with iron: having performed the purification by means of the three truths in both direct and reverse order, a person [should proceed].
Having placed eight auspicious cloths upon the excellent seat, he should wear them; *Oṃ dīrghāyustvā*.
With the *kaṅkayinī* mantra, with the *saṃpyāya* mantra, and with words of benediction, one should wrap the girl with a thread.
Oṃ, one should wrap it with a protective thread. Oṃ, you are the purifier; in the shadow of the noose. Oṃ, the purifier of wealth.
In the shade of Mount Śiṃdhara: Oṃ, may Śrī and Lakṣmī be yours. Añjana: Oṃ, that indeed is the divine razor.
A pair of udumbara fruits: *Oṃ śivo nāmāsi*. Three blades of kuśa grass: *Oṃ brahmaṇaspate*.

The *luṃkhopā*, the *ohokhopā*, and the *muḍu*. *Oṃ hiraṇyagarbha*. *Oṃ ayamūrjāvato vṛkṣa ūrjāvaphalānī bhavata*. Having heard [this], the bride [receives] sandalwood and other items, along with blessings. *Oṃ śrīvacchaśvamā*. For the offering (*āhuti*): *Oṃ sapta ṛṣayaḥ*. Offering. *Oṃ manojāti*. Consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*).
The offering of the sacrificial porridge (caru) in due order.
The Brahmin shall recite the Svastivācana.
Again, on the northern part of the sacrificial lion-throne, [offer] the oblation: *Oṃ ākṛṣṇena*. *Yahamālā tvāya*.
O garland of planets! Oṃ, you are the swiftest; you were born for the sake of generating the auspiciousness of the youthful jar in the sacrificial pavilion.
The oblation offered to Kumārakalaśa: Oṃ, [offering] to Jatrapānāsaṃpata. To Kumāra Brāhmaṇacālaṃsīya, to Thaṃkādin, to Nṛvacchanādi Paripāthin, and to Lāsālahe.
A woman does not go to the swift, shaven-headed monks who have attained self-mastery within their own bodies.

The bride should hear the sound of the bamboo flute and the offering of oblations. "Oṃ! Now, let the King of the Āhāvins and the Nāginī sing together. This is the verse they recite when the appointed woman has been joined [in marriage], saying: "May he who is another hero-maker [protect us]."

The word *vena*. The oblation: *Oṃ*. This Vena, born of the speckled womb, the light within the amniotic membrane, in the expanse of the mid-air—may he, the infant at the meeting point of the sun, protect me; the wise ones overcome the fearful. *Gīta*.
The Oblation: Oṃ, you are the Veda born from the Veda;
as the Veda for the gods and for all deities, may you become the Veda for me.
The five sounds of the mṛdaṅga drum and other instruments. An oblation: *Oṃ namaḥ saṃbhavāya*. For the delight of the heroes' tales. An oblation:
*Oṃ saṃ tvam agne sūryasya varcasāgathāḥ, sam ṛṣīṇāṃ stutena. Saṃ priyeṇa dhāmnā, sam aham āyuṣā saṃ varcasā saṃ prajayā saṃ rāyaspoṣeṇa gmiṣīya.*
Nārāyaṇa is the sacrificer; he is the oblation in the great fire; he is the foundation.

For the offering of the tender and beautiful [food] (*dāna*); for the worship of the youth (*kumāra*) and the Brahmin; [the offering of] the seat and so forth, the water for the hands (*argha*), the garments and so forth, the ornaments, the red sandalwood and so forth, and ending with the lamps—these are not to be given to a man. [The formula begins with] "Today, like Bālāhaka... and so forth, starting from "today" and so on—the ritual statement (*vākya*).

To you, O young Brahmin of such-and-such lineage and such-and-such name, I give this *kumāra-kalaśa* (youth-vessel), filled with gold, accompanied by unbroken grains (*akṣata*), an umbrella, and cloth, for the sake of obtaining a son. [This is] the formula for the gift.

The Brāhmaṇa shall recite the *kodāt* [mantra]. The *anna-saṃkalpa* [is performed]. Gold is the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). Men and women [receive] blessings (*āśīrvāda*). The Brāhmaṇa shall recite hymns of praise (*stuti*). For the man, [he shall recite] the *Puruṣasūkta*. And for the boy, the Brāhmaṇa shall recite the *Vatsacchavi*.
A man stands before a woman. The worship and adoration of Keśava according to the Śvetavidhi rite.

Having performed the *ācamana*, [one proceeds] for the *arghya* offering to the Sun, for the ritual placement (*nyāsa*), the worship of the *arghya* vessel, and self-worship. *Oṃ tat savitur vareṇyam*. *Oṃ devasya tvā*. *Oṃ gaṇānāṃ tvā*. *Oṃ bṛhaspate*. *Oṃ*.
O Goddess, you who have four horns, Oṃ! Oṃ! Viṣṇu is this; Oṃ! Śrī is yours, Lakṣmī is yours.
Oṃ, to the Support-Power (Ādhāraśakti); to the seat of Ananta; to the lotus-seat (Padmāsana); to the filaments (Keśara); to the pericarp (Karṇikā).
To Garuḍāsana; to Viṣṇu.
meditative absorption (dhyāna)
Oṃ, I meditate upon that god who eternally possesses four arms, with Lakṣmī seated upon his left side, the perpetual destroyer of the Daityas, and the bestower of all spiritual accomplishments.
To Keśava; to Nārāyaṇa; to Śrīdevī; to Lakṣmīdevī; to Maṅgalā.

Salutation to Maṅgalā. Oṃ juṃjate, etc. Oṃ, you are the beautiful-winged Garuḍa; Oṃ, you are the sword; Oṃ, the golden one; Oṃ, you two are the purifiers; Oṃ, you are auspicious by name; Oṃ, for us, O Indra; Oṃ, well-kindled, Guṃ.
Oṃ śrīścate lakṣmī. Catusvasti. Oṃ dhūrasi. Oṃ tejosi. Oṃ japhalanī. Oṃ annapate. Oṃ manojoti. Jāpa. Stuti.
Oṃ, O Lord of Lakṣmī, salutations to you, the bestower of all prosperity,
the granter of desires and liberation, and the giver of wealth and sons.
The hand of Jayā; [the mantra] beginning with "pāpohaṃti" and so forth; likewise, sandalwood and other offerings; and worship according to the white rite.
She stands on the northern side of the Jajñasiṃhāsana. [At the parting of the hair: *Śīmantani*. [The oblation:
*Oṃ māhirbhūrmāpṛdā kurnnamasta ātānānarvā prehi | ghṛtasya kulyā uparitasya pathyā anu svāhā*. [The oblation: *Oṃ manojoti pratiṣṭhā*. Having heard [the name] of the bride: "Amukadevī."
"May she be blessed with sons! Oṃ! By the sovereignty of Soma, may human progeny be turned toward us;
may there be long life for you who are present at the banks of the Āśīra, the Ayovā, and the Vāgvatī. Having heard these words, the bride—

The Brahmin worship; the rites for pacification and nourishment; the offering of *kuśa* grass and the sequence of *javadhāna* and other oblations; the construction of the auspicious *śumaṇḍha* and the eight auspicious symbols (*aṣṭamaṅgala*) within the mandala; the kindling of the fire; the dismissal of the fire; and the offering of the sacrificial bali.
The consecration of the sacrificer and others, the pronouncement of blessings, the *sepha* rite, the *ārathi* rite, and the vision of the Virgin Goddess (*komāri-darśana*).
For the sake of having the sun as witness; for the worship of Keśava by the Brāhmaṇa; may there be auspiciousness at every step. Thus ends the rite of the parting of the hair (Sīmantonnayana).
Now, the rite for completing the month: on an auspicious day, the bride, having bathed, [takes] a vessel of flowers.

The worship of the *kalaśa* (water-pot); the *sagona*; the *gaṇa*, the cow-portion (*gogrāsa*), and the offering (*bali*) to Kaumārī—these one should worship with a Brāhmaṇa. *Oṃ tat savitur vareṇyam*, etc. Worship of the door; worship of the *kalaśa*; worship of the *sagona*. *Oṃ ā kṛṣṇena*, etc.;
*Oṃ trātāram indram*, etc.; *Oṃ aśvastheyā*, etc. [Worship of] the month and the lunar mansion; the worship of the *bali*.
What kind of worship is this, which causes only pain?
Gaṇapati, Gogrāsa, Kaumārīpūjā, Ākāśamāla, Hnasakana.
Sindhu-rāmūṅga || Fourfold Auspiciousness || Incense || Lamp || Fruit || Food Offering || Consecration || Recitation of Mantras ||
Hymn of praise; worship of the Brahmins; one should recite the Śāntika [rite]; worship of Metamphantāda.
The bridegroom and the bride enter the hall; they gaze upon the auspicious, all-pervading wheel; the people behold them.

For the purpose of purifying the *argha* vessel: "O woman about to give birth, sprinkle her with water: Just as the wind causes the lotus pond to stir on every side, so may your fetus move, and may it come forth with the afterbirth.
This stall for Indra has been prepared—enclosed and well-fenced; O Indra, drive [the child] out from there."
[The mantra] for the protection of the womb: *saheti*. For the removal of one's own [faults]: *svānataṃnake*. For the rite of pacification (*śāntika*): *svānaviye*.
Having struck this bell for the sake of the dance of the deities, [I offer] the blessing with sandalwood and other substances.
The offering of betel leaves for his worship, as well as the gift of a young banyan tree and other such items.

Oṃ, I approach according to reality. Oṃ, by the impulse of the god. Oṃ, you, O Agni, with the [oblations]. Oṃ, O Prajāpati. Oṃ, Lord of Food. Oṃ, born of mind. The Brahmin’s declaration of intent regarding the food: In the lineage of Puruṣanaja, of the Bhonaṭva clan, descended from Vadhula; in the Pāṭanavāra branch of the Saguṇadhari family; at Ucchiṣṭakaraṅkacchaya.
Laṃṣana-hāye || Benediction || Oṃ annapate || Oṃ manojoti || Consecration || Dakṣiṇā ||

The hundred water-pot recitations; the blessing from the water pot; the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and dismissal of the offerings (*balivisarjana*); the entire ceremony including the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) and blessings; the procession with the phallus (*liṅga*) by a man; and the viewing of the virgin (*kumārī*).
Having established Thaṃkā and others as witnesses, he brought five hundred men and women from Sāntika.
For the purpose of the perpetual worship of Keśava. Thus ends the complete procedure for the month.

Now, the birth-rite (*jātakarman*). Having performed the shaving of the head (*kṣaura*) and the *nārāyaṇa* rite on the day of birth, and having concluded with the *puṃsavana*, the father first performs the ritual bathing (*snāna*) with *thaṃka* and other substances, offers the water for the *nāndīmukha* ancestors, and then proceeds with the *thaṃka* and other rites.
The worship of the water-pot by the Brahmin.

Bhucāsa, Kakuḍa, Toyukāpaḍago, and Kāṃlovaṃpa—these are all the deities who reside there. [One should perform] the single oblation with clarified butter: *oṃ tat sat* and so forth. [This includes] the worship of the planet, the consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*), the recitation (*jāpa*), the hymn (*stotra*), the worship of the Brahmins, the rites for peace (*śāntika*), the rites for prosperity (*pauṣṭika*), and the benediction from the Brahmins. Brahmin.

The resolution regarding the food (*anna-saṃkalpa*), the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), and the offering of oblations (*bali-haraṇa*); the father shall wear two washed garments; having sat upon a *svastika* seat facing east; [the performance of] the *nṛ-vamśa-śānti*; the remainder of the consecration (*kalaśābhiṣeka*); and the recitation of the *jalamyālā-sūkta*, etc.

The father performs the consecration (*abhiṣeka*). [He applies] sandalwood paste and other substances to the body. [He offers] blessings (*āśīrvāda*). [He performs] the *ārati* ritual. At the place of birth, the father shall go to the Brāhmaṇas. For the purpose of crossing over the "river of impurity" (*jalimiyālā satayālaṅghana*), [he acts] with the father’s hand. The mantra: *oṃ ejatudasamāsyo garbhājarāyunā saha | yathāyaṃ vāpurejati | yathā samudra ejati ||* "O embryo, ten months old, move forth along with the afterbirth! Just as this wind moves, just as the ocean moves."

Thus has this ten-month-old [embryo] been released along with the placenta. *Oṃ*, whose these sacrificial embryos are, whose golden womb is, and whose limbs are uninjured—that measure [of the body], may it come together;
*guṃ svāhā*. The mantra for sprinkling again: *Oṃ*, may the speckled one attend to me.
The remainder should be given to the dog for the sake of the fetus. Let her not eat it; let no fisherwoman take anything from it.
May the vajra-nectar descend. One should perform the bath for the prince while the umbilical cord is still uncut.

With the ring finger and thumb, using a *lavaṅga* (cloves) ladle covered with ghee, honey, and gold, one should offer [the mixture] for consumption. The mantra is: *oṃ bhūs tvayi dadhāmi*; *oṃ bhuvas tvayi dadhāmi*; *oṃ svas tvayi dadhāmi*;
*oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ sarvaṃ tvayi dadhāmi*. The youth, having performed the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*), [should consume it].
The Sandalwood and Other Blessings: Having touched the boy’s right ear with the mantra:
*Oṃ agnirāyuṣmān sa vanaspatībhirāyuṣmāṃstena tvāyuṣāyuṣmantaṃ karomi.* *Oṃ soma āyuṣmān sa oṣadhībhirāyuṣmāṃstena tvāyuṣāyuṣmantaṃ karomi.*
Oṃ! Brahman is life; that which belongs to the brahmins is life. By means of that life, O long-lived one, I make you long-lived.
Oṃ! O long-lived one, by means of that life-force of yours which is immortal, I make you long-lived through that very life-force.
Oṃ! The sages are long-lived; they are long-lived through their vows. By that longevity, I make you long-lived.

Oṃ! The ancestors are long-lived; they are long-lived through their *svadhās*. By that longevity, I make you long-lived. Oṃ! The sacrifice is long-lived; it is long-lived through its sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇās*). By that longevity, I make you long-lived. Oṃ! The ocean is long-lived; it is long-lived through its flowing currents. By that...

"O Venerable One, I grant you a threefold lifespan. [This is] the mantra for touching [the child] again on the ear: *oṃ* tryāyuṣaṃ jamagneḥ kaśyapasya tryāyuṣam | yad deveṣu tryāyuṣaṃ tan no astu tryāyuṣam || "Oṃ!
May there be the threefold lifespan of Agni, the threefold lifespan of Kaśyapa; may that threefold lifespan which exists among the gods be ours."

He touches his ear with the mantra: *Oṃ, if he should desire, "May he live a full span of life. Oṃ, you are Iḍā; Mitra and Varuṇa have generated you as a hero for a heroic son. May you be possessed of heroes, for you shall grant us prosperity.* Then, again, with the father's hand, he touches the boy’s speech.
Mantra: Oṃ. From heaven, Agni was first at the sacrifice; Jātavedas was the second.
The third time he was in the waters, the wise one who kindles him unceasingly praises him, being well-disposed in mind.
Oṃ! We know your three limbs in three ways; we know your abodes distributed in many places.
We know your supreme name which is hidden in the secret cave; we know the source from which you have come forth.

Oṃ! The manly-minded one kindled you within the waters, the sea; the observer of men kindled you at the udder of heaven’s summit. In the third realm, the mighty ones have strengthened you who stand upon the earth, in the lap of the wide expanse.
Oṃ! Agni has roared like the thundering sky; he has overspread the earth and anointed the plants.
As soon as he was born, kindled, he looked abroad; he has filled the two worlds, shining from his central navel.
Magnificent bestower of glories, supporter of riches, inspirer of inspired thoughts, guardian of Soma, the Vasu,
the Son of Strength, the King of the Waters, he shines forth at the forefront of the Dawns, kindled with fuel.
Oṃ! The banner of the universe, the germ of the world, he filled the two worlds (heaven and earth) upon being born;
he, the wise one, cleaves the mountain for wealth for the people—he who has generated Agni, the five tribes.
Oṃ! The wise Agni, the immortal messenger among mortals, has been established as one who is sought.
Bearing aloft his ruddy smoke, he hastens forward, reaching the heavens with his bright, consuming flame.

Oṃ! Like the sun, he has shone across the wide earth; his life is irrepressible, and he blazes with splendor for the sake of glory. Through his vital powers, Agni became immortal when Dyaus, rich in seed, brought him forth.
O God Agni of auspicious luster, whoever today has prepared for you the sacrificial cake rich in ghee—
lead him further toward greater wealth, and, most active one, grant him the favor bestowed by the gods.
O Agni, grant a share in the invocations for glory; at every hymn, grant us a portion in our dwelling.
Be beloved by Sūrya, be beloved by Agni; through that power, may he break through and be born anew.
Oṃ! Day after day, O Agni, the sacrificers have bestowed upon you all desirable riches and noble boons.
Desiring wealth through you, the seekers have opened up the cow-filled stall.
One should recite the eleven verses beginning with "Oṃ. The father recites the mantra: "Oṃ, may I breathe after this one. Again, the officiant (yajamāna), facing east, should speak the mantra:
"Oṃ, the vital breaths (prāṇāḥ). Facing south, he should speak the mantra: "Oṃ, the downward breaths (apānāḥ). [Facing] west... Oṃ.

The Vyānas. One should recite the mantra facing north: *Oṃ udānaḥ*. In the middle, one should recite the mantra facing upward: *Oṃ samānāḥ*. The mantra for touching the newborn child at the place where the father [holds him]: *Oṃ vedate bhūmi hṛdayaṃ divi candramasi śritam*.
"I know that; may we see a hundred autumns;
may I live for a hundred autumns; may we hear for a hundred autumns. Then the father, touching the boy with his hand, [recites] the mantra for the first holding:
"Oṃ, from this [child] become an axe, become gold, become immortal; become the Self."

May he live for a hundred autumns, his son named Vapu. [The officiant] consecrates the mother of the boy with the mantra: "Oṃ! You are Iḍā, you are Maitrāvaruṇī; as a hero, you have given birth to a hero. May you be possessed of heroes, and may you make us possessed of heroes.
Then, by means of the sacrificer, the right breast of the mother is washed for the boy.

He gives the mantra: *Oṃ imaṃ guṃ stanaṃ ūrjaṃ svatandhayāyāṃ prapīnam agne śarīrasya madhye | utsaṃ juṣasva madhumantam arvvaṃ samudriyaṃ guṃ sadanam āviśasva*. Again, having washed with the left hand, [he recites] the mantra: *Oṃ yaste stanaḥ*.

Sarasvatī, who is full of abundance, made of gold, a further bestower of jewels, the knower of wealth, and the giver of good gifts— by her, the one who possesses all life, may auspicious noble deeds flow here for us alone.
The mantra for placing the water-pot at the head of the Prince’s bed.

Oṃ! O Waters, be watchful among the gods; as you are watchful among the gods, so be watchful over this woman who has given birth, over her who has well-begotten a daughter. Then follows the cutting of the umbilical cord. A Brāhmaṇa should recite the *svastivācana* (invocation of well-being). The father should perform the ritual bath. The father [performs] the consecration and other rites, including the bestowing of blessings. Thus ends the *jātakarman* (birth-rite).
It is finished.
Then, having established the birth-fire at the doorway.
Installation facing east. Water offering for the Sun (*sūryārgha*). The ritual placement (*nyāsa*) with the *ākṛṣṇena* verse from the *Gāyatrī*. The water-offering vessel (*arghapātra*).

Self-worship (*ātmapūjā*). Oṃ *jadevādeva*. Oṃ *mānastoke*. Oṃ *tattvā yāmi*. The upholding of the *Gāyatrī*. Oṃ *sadasaspati*. Oṃ *bhīrhayaśca me*. Oṃ *devasya tvā*. Oṃ *hiraṇyagarbha*. Oṃ *padmānire*.

Oṃ, you are splendor. Oṃ, the slayer of demons. Oṃ, golden-hued one. Oṃ, for your immortality. Oṃ, kindling you. Oṃ, you are the seasons. Oṃ, Agni is the head. Oṃ, the flesh-eating Agni. Oṃ, Agni follows the dawns. Having recited thus, [recite] "Oṃ, may my houses be foremost. The recitation of blessings (*svastivācana*). Oṃ, my vital organs. Oṃ.
Facing west, [one performs] the seat of the Veda: *oṃ agnim īḷe*, etc. This is the worship of the beginning of the Vedas.

Worship of the World-Protectors (*lokapāla*). *Oṃ*, obeisance to the Fire of Childbirth (*sūtikāgni*). *Oṃ*, this is the God; [I invoke him] here. *Oṃ*, obeisance to Mahīdhara. Accept this offering (*bali*), *svāhā*. [Perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*) and other rites. *Oṃ*, obeisance to Kāmadeva. *Oṃ*, obeisance to the form (*mūrti*) of Kāmadeva. *Oṃ*, obeisance to Kāmadeva. [Offer] the *bali*. [Perform] the invocation (*āvāhana*) and other rites. *Oṃ*.

Salutation to Pragalbhāgniyāsanam. Oṃ, salutation to Pragalbhāgnimūrti. Oṃ, salutation to Pragalbhāgni. [Offer] the bali. [Perform] the invocation (āvāhana) and other rites. One should offer oblations with *samidh* sticks of two *dāḍima* trees using the mantra "Oṃ Kālena."

One black [oblation]. An oblation of clarified butter: *Oṃ śaṇḍāmarkā upavīraḥ śauṇḍikeya unmūṣalaḥ | malimlū codroṇāsaścyavamānaścyatāditiḥ svāhā*. Again, the mantra for the oblation: *Oṃ ālikhannanimiṣaḥ kiṃ vadanta upaśrutiḥ | haryakṣa...*

"May the one with the face of a jar, the enemy, the vessel, the abyss, the pit, the mouthless, the harsh as chaff, and the destroyer perish—Iditi, Svāhā! Then, perform the fuel-wood oblation (samidh-homa): offer one with the syllable *Oṃ* and one silently.

Ghee-oblation. Gaṇa. Guru. Durgā. Kṣetrapāla. Vyāhṛtis. Veda. Lokapālas. To the Fire of Childbirth, Svāhā! Om, to Mahīdhara, Svāhā! Om, to Kāmadeva, Svāhā! Om, to Pragalbhāgni, Svāhā! Vyāhṛti-dhāra. Om, seven are your [tongues], O Agni... Ghee-oblation, full.
One should offer oblations mixed with small grains, mustard roots, and seeds to Gaṇeśa, Guru, and Durgā.
Kṣetrapāla, Vyāhṛti, Veda, Lokapāla, Śūtikāgni, Mahīdhara, Kāmadeva.
The bold one; the sustainer of speech; the oblations of *saṃkṣā*, *śāntika*, and *puṣṭika*; the full offering (*pūrṇā*); the single invocation;
*Oṃ pūrṇādavardhipa*; the conclusion; and the benediction (*āśīrvāda*)—these are the [rites] to be performed with the *nakakohnu*.

Daily worship at the time of the junction of the two halves of the day. Having performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), the offering to the Sun (sūryārgha), and the ritual placement of mantras (gāyatrī-nyāsa).
Worship of the Arghya Vessel || Self-Worship || Oṃ, I go to the Truth || The Seat || Oṃ, [I take] you, belonging to the God.
Sprinkling: *Oṃ tvā vṛtte*. Sprinkling the wood: *Oṃ indhānās tvā*. Sharpening: [silence].
For the performance of the *homa* sacrifice according to the ritual procedure: [offer] with the milk of a cow. Oṃ, we know the source of the golden-hued one.
They have known the known; they have placed the powerful one in the womb for the sake of release. May he enter the womb of the sheep.
Thus ends the section on the Sūtikāgni (the birth-fire).
Then, on the sixth day, having performed the vigil and worship for Viṣṇu, [one should perform] the Kumāla-bath.

The rite for the dismissal of the offerings (*baliviśarjanayāṅga*) to Keśava; the rite for the bathing (*snānayāṅga*) of Nārāyaṇa; furthermore, [the rites for] Nārāyaṇa, the water-pot (*kalaśa*), the birth-chart (*janmapatrikā*), Gaṇeśa, and the morsels for the cows (*gogrāsa*).
The maiden [is] powerful; having established the external linga, the youth [is] on the finger.

One should worship at the door-jambs and the base of the pillar during the evening. According to one's capacity, [offerings should be made] to the Brāhmaṇas, the flower-vessels, the mendicants, the *thaṃkāḍins*, and into the hand of the one beginning with *Oṃ*. [Offer] the *arghya* water. Perform the *gāyatrī-nyāsa*.

Self-worship with the *argha* vessel: *Oṃ tat tvā yāmi*. One should worship with the twelve [names] beginning with Keśava and the twelve powers (*śakti*) beginning with Śrī; with the twelve [verses] beginning with *Oṃ divo vā*; and with the power-verse (*śakti-ṛc*) beginning with *Oṃ śrīścate*. [Then] *Oṃ trātāram indra...* and so forth. Viṣṇu-ratha.

Worship. Here [are the offerings of] fragrance and so forth. Worship of the water-pot (*kalaśa*). *Oṃ brahma yajñāna...* and so forth. *Oṃ ā kṛṣṇena...* and so forth. Here [are the offerings of] fragrance and so forth. Worship of the birth-chart (*janmapatrikā*). *Oṃ tā asa...* and so forth. *Oṃ aśvastha co...* and so forth. *Oṃ arddhamāsa...* and so forth. Worship of the outer courtyard. With their respective mantras.

*Catuḥsvasti*, etc. | *Oṃ dhūr asi* | *Oṃ tejo 'si*. Having lit one hundred and eight lamps before the deity: *Oṃ mano jyotiḥ*. Consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*), recitation (*jāpa*), hymn (*stotra*), and worship of the Brāhmaṇas beginning with Keśava. One should recite the *Śāntika* [hymns]. At the recitation of blessings (*svastivācana*): *Oṃ krandasva* | *Oṃ āśuḥ śiśānaḥ* | *Oṃ jajñānaḥ* | *Sahasraśīrṣā*. *Oṃ*.
The body of Agni: *oṃ vaya tuṃso*. Worship of the sixty temples in the place of birth: *oṃ tatvāyāmi*, *oṃ devasya tvā*, *oṃ śivāyai namaḥ*, *oṃ viśvataścakṣuḥ*, *śambhūtyai*, *oṃ tāṃ guṃ savituḥ*.
For the sake of joy: *Oṃ dyāmālekṣī*—for the sake of continuity. *Oṃ ambe ambike*—for the sake of Anusutā. *Oṃ catvāriśṛṅgā*—for the sake of Kṣamā. *Oṃ āmidrarīdra śīrākumālasa*.
Oṃ yatravānā. Here [are offered] perfumes and so forth. Japa. Stotra. Oṃ śivāsaṃbhūti. Nāmā, Prītisaṃtati, Anusūyā, and Akṣamā—these six are the sixty deities.

Just as Skanda, the son of Gaurī, protects children, so may this child of mine be protected by the Ṣaṣṭhī deity. Here [are offered] perfumes and other items. Obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, the protector of the sacrificer, the self-restrained one, the one of great luster; obeisance to the Arghya. *Oṃ agnimūrdhā*. [Nyāsa].
|| Arghapātra-pūjā || Ātma-pūjā || Oṃ dyau śānti || Śāntika svānaviye ||
The *svāhāntaka* [mantra], the *japa*, the *stotra*, the *anna-saṃkalpa*, the *dakṣiṇā*, the *bali*, and the dismissal (*visarjana*) of the *maitra*.
The Nārāyaṇabali rite for the purpose of deluding [the enemy]; the consecration with the water-pot (kalaśābhiṣeka); and the benediction with sandalwood paste and other substances.
For the sake of joy at birth, for the sake of joy at delusion. [This is] the Brāhmaṇa’s Kalaśa-jātaka; by which it was the place of birth.
The meal for the Brahmins. Thus ends the ritual procedure for the sixth day.
Then, at the time of dawn, one should perform the circumambulation.

To the left, having placed a vessel [filled with] *kalaguḍī* (a type of plant), one should offer *plakā*, meat, and *sesā* (sesame) along with unbroken rice balls (*akṣata-gola*). This is the ritual for Vasundharā; it should not be performed by anyone else.
Having performed the placement (nyāsa) upon the smoke-bellows, one should offer the oblation and release the powerful [deity] for the sake of dismissal.

*Balāṅgaharaṇa*: "O you who wear a garland of sky-flowers, please be seated. *Arghanyāsa*. *Arghapātrapūjā*.
Oṃ *tattvāyām* and so forth; Oṃ *imaṃ me gaṅge*; the invocation (*āvāhana*) and other rites; Oṃ *ākṛṣṇena*; Oṃ *trātāram indra*; Oṃ *asvastiv o*; Oṃ *ardhamāsā*; Oṃ *nakṣatrebhya*; Oṃ *yoge yoge*.

Bali offering: Oṃ gaṇānāṃ tvā; Oṃ jātavedase; Oṃ imā rudrāya; Oṃ ghṛtaṃ ghṛtapāvānaḥ; Oṃ namo babhruśāya. [Offer] the first *bali*. Oṃ viśvataścakṣuḥ. [Offer] rice. Oṃ bṛhadyaśśca me; Oṃ asmākam indra. One should recite the four *svasti* verses. Oṃ dhūr asi; Oṃ tejo 'si; Oṃ manaḥ.

Salutations to the jar that is the form of the earth, which, by means of Viṣṇu in the form of a digit, supports the entire foundation and is the source of all auspiciousness.

Herein, the incense and other offerings: *Oṃ yatravānā*, *lohocāsa*. *Oṃ yasya kūrmmaḥ*, *kāpaleśa*. *Oṃ ajārepi saṃgilāśvāvitkurupisaṃgilā | śasa āskaṃdamarubhyayi paṃthāmvisarpyati || ḍhomacalasasa*. *Oṃ tvaṃjaviṣṭadā*, *vājana*, *hāsāsapuvāke*.

Having risen from the seat, one should perform the preliminary rites such as the *tīrthodvāsa* (ritual dismissal of the sacred water). Then, having donned yellow garments and holding a conch shell and other implements, one should recite the *svastivācana* (invocation of well-being) for the Brahmin. This is performed during the *hāyadhunaṅāvahlāhlāyana*.
Having brought this *eyolaṅanaphicaka* vessel, which is a *gānaṅayaka* made from *mocā* bark, for the sake of the one who has been consecrated (*moḍakīnita*), [place] it upon the vessel.

[The sacrificer] mounts the chariot-pole, [desiring] vigor, strength, and longing. At the Kaṇḍipuya, for the sake of prosperity, [he recites] the Veda: "Oṃ! Having been consecrated, ascend the eastern direction; may the Gāyatrī protect you, the *Ṛgveda* as the *Sāman*, the *Trivṛt-stoma*, Soma, the spring season, and the Brahmin-class as your wealth. Ascend the southern direction; may the Triṣṭubh protect you..."
The *bṛhat* sāman, the fifteenfold soma-rite, the summer season, the ruling power, and wealth—these are the western ascent;
the *jagatī* metre, the *svāra* chant, the *vairūpa* sāman, the seventeenfold soma-rite, the rainy season, and various riches—these are the northern ascent; the *anuṣṭubh* metre, you...
The Caturvairāja Sāman, the Ekaviṃśa Stoma, the autumn season, and the fruit is wealth.

With ascending series of verses, with the Catuṣṭoma and the Sākvara, with the two Sāmans, the Raivata and the Śākvara, with the Triṇava and the Trayastriṃśa Stomas—[I have placed] the Hemanta and Śiśira seasons, luster, and wealth [within you]; the head of Namuci has been cast down.

O you who are the essence of the Veda,

the pure, the one without beginning or end, the stainless, the supreme, the one who dwells within the heart— do not take away my child. Oṃ, Brahman, the source of knowledge, the first-born, established by the light of the mind.
To those who pray for the sight of the sun: Oṃ, that and the razor, O God; lāsālāva; thaṃluvaṃne; the offering of worship is complete.
The procedure for the exit with the *dakṣiṇā* is completed. The consecration (*abhiṣeka*).
Then one should perform the naming ceremony.

The installation of the *kalaśa* is performed facing east. One should place the *golakas* (small balls) at the house of the cowherd, and likewise the *nāmacoyelun*. If the *kalaśa* faces west, one should offer a hundred oblations (*śatahoma*). As long as it is not [properly] established, one should perform the *svagvaṇa* rite; then, having offered the *toṃpo*, one should present the *naṅa* and the *bali*.
Like a plank, he is the offering in the mouth of the eater.
Alas! Even though he was compassionate toward those who sought refuge in him, he has now departed; what a sorrowful fate! What a tragedy!

The one who bestows life, the one who has gone to the peak of Mount Kailāsa, the one who dwells in the sky, the one who is adorned with serpents, the Lord of Gaṇas, and the one who accepts a morsel of cow's grass.

Komārī. These [offerings] such as the bull and so forth are placed upon the flower-vessel. According to the ritual for the worship of the pitcher (kalaśa) by the Brāhmaṇa, there is the recitation (jāpa), the hymn of praise (stotra), and the worship of the Brāhmaṇa.
One should recite the *sāntika* [rite]. This is the *metaṃphaṃ* offering with *tāḍacā*. *Lāsālāvahe*. *Mothaṃkādina*.
To him who delights in the lineage, who acts for the sake of the human race, who is the destroyer of the enemy, and who is the ornament of the vessel of honor.
For the sounding of the self-nature; for the peace of the celestial realm, for the sounding of the self-nature;
for the striking of this vessel, for the non-arising of attachment; for the offering-vessel, for the purification of the defilements; for the clothing, for the covering of the limbs;

for the shadow of the sacrificial offering, for the application of sandalwood and other fragrances; for the enclosure of the cattle, for the opening of the gate; for the physical body, for the attainment of immortality.
O Vahna-sasa! Hmyāca-jura-sāṣa, you who are named Vahna-sasa! Do not strike us; O Ghela-suya!

The mantra for the five morsels of food: A Brāhmaṇa should recite the *svastivācana* (benediction). [The removal of] the shadow of arrival, the stain of impurity from leftovers, the licking, the tasting, and the birthplace. At the naming ceremony (*nāmakaraṇa*), there is the blessing: *oṃ kāya svāhā*, *kusau svāhā*, *katamasmai svāhā*.
Svāhā to him who is meditated upon with devotion, svāhā! Svāhā to Prajāpati, the mind;
svāhā to Aditi, the knower of consciousness, svāhā! Svāhā to Mahī Aditi, svāhā to Aditi the very compassionate, svāhā to Sarasvatī!

Svāhā! To Sarasvatī the Purifying, Svāhā! To Sarasvatī the Vast, Svāhā! To Pūṣan, Svāhā! To Pūṣan on the Path, Svāhā! To Pūṣan the Protector, Svāhā! To Tvaṣṭṛ, Svāhā! To Tvaṣṭṛ the Shedder of Seed, Svāhā! To Tvaṣṭṛ of Many Forms, Svāhā! To Viṣṇu, Svāhā!

*Viṣṇave nibhūyapāya svāhā*. *Viṣṇavasiṣiviṣṭāya svāhā*. The light of the mind (*manojyoti*) is the foundation. The resolve for food (*annasaṃkalpa*). The sacrificial fee (*dakṣīnā*). The recitation of the *laṃṣakale-sasate*. Here, the Brahmins and others [receive] the perfumes and other offerings. The jar (*kalaśa*), the benediction (*āśīrvāda*), the ritual placement (*nyāsa*), the offering of oblations (*bali*), and the dismissal (*visarjana*). Then, from the *thaṃka* onwards...

The ritual consecration with the water-pot (*kalaśābhiṣeka*); the blessing (*āśīrvāda*) accompanied by sandalwood paste and other offerings; the offering of the *arathī*; the vision of the maiden (*komārī-darśana*); the full moon (*pūrṇacandra*); the entry through the excellent gate (*varaṅgata-dvārasate*); the circumambulation (*ḍokeviya*); and the presence of witnesses (*sākṣithāya*).
Salutations to Thaṃkādī and the others, who bring joy.
Thus ends the ritual for the naming ceremony.

Then, at six months, one should perform the *phalaprāsana* (the first feeding of fruit) and the *annaprāsana* (the first feeding of solid food). [The rites for] the child’s bath (*kumāra-snāna*), the *kalaśa* (vase), and the *śagvana* (consecration) are to be performed.
The Gaṇas, the cow-grazing [deities], the Komaṛīs, the Vahiragaṇas, and the Kevo-coyas; they dance in the midst of the assembly of those who have performed penance.
