For the purpose of the Jātūnaṭva rite: [the child] arrives at the Svastika-seat, adorned with the eight auspicious signs (aṣṭamaṅgala) such as the Śrīvatsa and others. [This is for] the Annaprāśana; the mantra for the five morsels (pañcagrāsa).

The Brahmin’s recitation of auspicious blessings (*svastivācana*): May there be well-being for the one who wears the garment of the Sugata; may there be well-being for the one whose body is like a lotus fiber; may there be well-being for the one who has never known the path of worldly existence; may there be well-being for the one who is free from the eight impurities; may there be well-being for the one who possesses the eight auspicious signs; may there be well-being for the one who has transcended all conceptual elaborations.

The Brahmin’s fee (brahmaṇadakṣiṇā); the recitation (vācana); the blessing of the water jar (kalaśa-āśīrvāda); the dismissal of the offerings (balivisarjana); the consecration with the water jar for the Thaṅkā and other items; the blessing of the auspicious materials such as sandalwood paste (caṃdana-ādi śagvana-āśīrvāda); the ceremonial scarf (sephaṃ); and the ritual circumambulation with the lamp (ārathī).

The vision of the Maiden (Komārī). The Full Moon. To bear witness. The lineage of Mocāpiṃtā. The seat, the umbrella, and the treasury of the progenitor. Thus ends the ritual for the first feeding of solid food (annaprāśana), which includes the offering of fruit.
The ritual procedure for the first feeding of solid food and the first feeding of rice, including the rite of re-initiation.
Even your father has departed; even all the kinsmen have departed. Having sat upon the funeral pyre and offered the libations, one should bow to that immediate radiance.
The throat-nectar is the nourishment; the five morsels are for the first day; the skull-bowl is the vessel for the remnants.
The ritual procedure for worship is exactly as previously described. Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the throat.
Then, having performed the tonsure ceremony, [one should perform] the midday offering for as many days as there are until the Brahmāduṃkā.
Then, on the following day, the *prohita* and others perform the worship of the *mālaka* and offer *javodaka*.

O Kumāralāsāladuta! Having first sat upon a svastika seat facing east, having performed the worldly customs such as bowing and salutation, and having offered the *sarabhṛṃdikā* oblation, one should cut the topknot (*śikhā*) and pluck out the hair of the fingers.
The rites for sandalwood and other substances, the benediction (*āśīrvāda*), the consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*), the *sepha* offering, the *ārati*, the *māsagheḍe*,
and the *lāsālavuṃ* performed at the birth of the Kumāra— these are the procedures for all subsequent days;
this is the procedure for the *vasapa* (concluding) rite on the day of peace (*saṃti*).
Brahmā, the eight vases, the Nāgas, the Yakṣas, the Yakṣiṇīs, Śrī Lakṣmī, the ritual of sacrifice,
Svānalāhālanathī, to the Yinyanaka, to the Anini-phaninakā, to the Yodakayāye.

Brahmā requested worship; by Śivācārya, in the ritual procedure, Kumāra was elevated; having performed the selection of the king and so forth, what is the fruit? [It is] the palm-leaf manuscript; together with the lineage; he praised the one who is the limit of the world.
Śucchāya; Caṇḍanādi-āśīrvāda; Pratiṣṭhā; Sefhaṃ; Ārathī; Māsadyeḍe; Lāsālāvayeneliviśa; Upatanayāya; Moṇḍahluyake.
For the purpose of the fire-rite (agnikārya), the worship of the eight jars (aṣṭakalaśa-pūjā) is performed by a Brāhmaṇa according to the rules and with mantras.

External worship of the gaṇas and others; the accomplishment of the meaningful words; the tenfold ritual of fire; the names of the fires: *Oṃ sadbhyaḥ agnaye svāhā*. Offerings of clarified butter (*ghṛta*); offerings of sesame seeds (*tila*); the purificatory offering (*saṃskāra-huti*) which one shakes off.

In a copper vessel containing *salākha* [rice], near the fire-pit (*agni-kuṇḍa*), they should offer oblations to the deities with yellow *piṃka* rice. Then, with curd, white sesame, and warm water, the mother of the child should bring them together. Having sat upon a *svastika* seat in the northern part of the sacrificial ground.

[The ritual begins with] the *nṛvaṃcchada* and so forth. The father, having taken cold water, pours it here into a vessel of hot water. [He recites: "O Vāyu, with this warm water, shave away the hair that has been struck by disease. Then the father again takes hot water.

The mantra for anointing the right side of the prince’s head: *Oṃ savitā prasūtā devyā āpa udantute tanuṃ cūṣavarān saṃkhiye*. The mantra for sprinkling *kuśa* grass and *udumbara* wood: *Oṃ dīrghāyustvā*. The mantra for [the blade]: *Oṃ oṣadhe trāyasva svadhite mainaṃ hiṃsīḥ sāṃḥ*.

|| Sūpapūjā || The mantra for the razor with a handle: Oṃ, you are named Śiva, the fire, the lightning; salutations be to you, O mother Guṃsī. The mantra for the razor at the time of shaving: Oṃ, I turn back [the razor] for the sake of long life, for the sake of food, for progeny, for wealth, for vigor, and for good offspring.
For heroic vigor.

The mantra for cutting the hair: *Oṃ, with that razor with which the wise Savitṛ [shaved] King Soma and Varuṇa, with that may the Brahman shave this [hair] of yours, so that it may be life-prolonging and reach old age.* [The hair is to be cut.]
[One should] sprinkle [the area]. It should be smeared with cow dung in the east. Furthermore, the mantra should be recited while offering [water] in the western part:

*Oṃ savitāprasūtā devyā āpa udantute tanuṃ*. The mantra for pouring [water] into the conch is: *Oṃ dīrghāyustvā*. The mantra for [placing] the *kuśa* grass, flowers, and *duṃbari* wood is: *Oṃ oṣadhetrāyasva*. *Oṃ*.
The blessing of the auspicious ones. Again, the mantra for the re-tying of the sacred thread: *Oṃ triyāyuṣaṃ jamadagneḥ*.

Having placed [the materials] in a vessel of cow dung, one should again recite the mantra over the northern part: *oṃ savitā prasavitā devyā āpa udantute tanuṃ*. For the counting of the excellent blades of grass (*kuśa*), the mantra is: *oṃ dīrghāyustvā*. For the collection of *kuśa* grass, flowers, and *udumbara* wood, the mantra is: *oṃ oṣadhe trāyasva*. *Oṃ*.

May Śiva be auspicious. Oṃ, may you return for the sake of long life. The mantra for the binding: Oṃ, by that same [power] by which Tvaṣṭṛ ascended to heaven and long beheld the sun from behind, by that sacred formula (brahman) I bind you, so that you may live, for your livelihood, for renown, and for well-being. [The cutting: Having placed it in a vessel of cow dung, [one should cut] the hair.
First, one should silently cut the hair upwards; then, having placed it in a vessel of cow dung.
The mantra for piercing the ears: *Oṃ bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ*. Then, the head of the boy [is touched].
The turning of the razor: *Oṃ, as the barber shaves with the razor, may he not cut the hair that has reached the head;

shave the hair, do not deprive him of his life-span.* The barber also recites this mantra while shaving the head with the razor: *Oṃ, one should shave around without cutting.* [He shaves] with the barber’s razor.

One should cut everything off. Having placed a vessel of cow dung, one should wash away the hair into the ocean. This is the bathing of the youth (*kumāra-snāna*). On the surface of the *moṇḍasa-golocana* [seat], at *lāsālahe*, having sat upon a swastika seat on the right side of the sacrificial throne (*yajñasiṃhāsana*), [one performs] the *nṛvaṃcchaṇa* and so forth, and having offered the water for the guest-offering (*arghapātra*) and the cloth.
Svānataṃnake || Metaṃphaṃ || Tāḍacā sagonanaṃṭvāya || Vastraviye ||
Sandalwood and other [fragrances], blessings; may there be the prosperity of Moṇḍasa; may there be the prosperity of Bhoyumala.

To the one who possesses a treasury of various vessels; whose shadow is like that of a peacock; who acts like a tortoise; who causes [the world] to be split open; who is not subject to the cycle of rebirth.
Hāsānagāle || [This is] the gift of Pasāda Pitīnivi, [made] for the Vandanavana. The oblation: Oṃ.

The gods generated Agni Vaiśvānara—the head of heaven, the navel of earth, born of truth, the sage, the sovereign, the guest of men, the vessel set upon the sacrificial grass—Oṃ. May auspiciousness come to our ears... Oṃ. The light of the mind...
Pratiṣṭhā, Sepha, Ārathi, Māsagheḍe, and Lāsālāvathaṃtayaṇa.
The Brahmin Worship for the New Year of the Snake: Peaceful rites, Prosperous rites, barley, grain, and so forth.
The resolve regarding food; the full sacrificial fee; aspiration; benediction; the offering of oblations.
The consecration by Brahmā; the blessing with sandalwood paste and other substances; the dismissal of the sacrifice; and the vision of Kumārī.
Kaleśahlāya || Yināyahlāya || Brahmā laṃṣanaluye || Thus ends the ritual procedure for the tonsure ceremony (cūḍākaraṇa).

Now, the rite for the *vaṭuka* [attendant spirits]: first, the purification through the daily service (*sevā*); then, the worship of the *pīṭha* [sacred seats]. Brahmā is in the *duṃkāya* [central channel]; the *hṅathva* [upper part] is the *kohnulu* [vessel] of the *siṃpāya* [offering].
To the family priest and others; to the forest of worship; to the one who goes with water; to the one who brings joy; to the one who has attained his own state.
Metaṃpha, tāḍacā, sagvana, naṭvāya, sarabhaṇḍikāvāya, candanādi.
Blessing: Oṃ manojyoti. Installation: Mepha ārathi. Māsagheḍe.
Lāsālāvathaṃtaṃyanne || Duṃśalajānake || This is the ritual procedure for this very day. |||1||
The ritual for the removal of misfortune (*saṃtikoṇuhāvidhi*): the Brahmā-vase, the Nāga-fragrance, the Yakṣa and Yakṣiṇī, and Śrī Lakṣmī.
Outside, on a *paṭapa* tree in the eastern direction: the ritual procedure for the *homa*; a staff of *palāśa* wood.
The staff of the Gaṃbhāli Ṛṣi; the black antelope skin; the yoga-mat; the *micakiṃhnasa*; the *muṃja* grass girdle.
Bhokholā-tahaṇḍagha || Luṃ-aṅguli || Oho-aṅguli || Vastra || These are the garments.

To the Leader (Yināyaka). Anina. Phanina. Kāya. Yodakayāya. For the worship of Brahmā (Brahmāpūjāyāya). Ṭinina. In the ritual of the eight directions starting from the east: Succhāya. Yaṃkulisa. Nṛvaṃcchana.
Having purified the *argha* vessel with *laṃ*, [recite] *svānataṃnake*, *metaṃphaṃ*, and *tāḍacā*.

For the sake of being free from all obstacles; for the sake of being sprinkled with the purifying waters; for the sake of auspiciousness. Oṃ, from every joint, from every joint... [Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad 1.3]... from joint to joint. Koḍa.
Oṃ, may you have long life! May there be the blessing of sandalwood and other fragrances for the sake of the gentle dance of the moon! Navahlāya! May there be the blessing of sandalwood and so forth!
Pratiṣṭhā, Sepha, Ārathi, Māsagheḍe, and Lāsālāvahleṅesa Svastikasate.

He requested a tooth-stick, he requested nail-clippers, he requested sixteen conch-shells, and he requested [materials for] bathing. Then, on the southern side of the sacrificial throne, having sat upon a hundred svastikas facing east, [he remained].

Having performed the worldly customs such as the *nṛvaṃcchana* [offering], [the presentation of] garments and ornaments, and [protection under] the shade of a serpent: *Oṃ trātāram indra sarabhaṇḍikāna koṣāyake*. *Oṃ ākṛṣṇe*. [The offering of] sandalwood paste and other items, along with benedictions: *anininaṭvāya*. *Oṃ śivo*.
Nāmāsi | Hāsānagāle | Oṃ tavavāyu vṛhaspato | Prasādapiṭiniviya |
In the forest of debate, [there is] establishment. Oṃ, may the radiance of the mind be offered as an oblation. To Māsagheḍa.
Lāsā, lāvathaṃtāyaṃne, phanina, vajinake, dadhilājā, ucchoṭacchoyā.
The tip of a serpent's hood.
Having offered the fire-oblation for the Guru, one should worship the eight jars beginning with Brahmā.
The accomplishment of the meaningful words: having taken the flowers for the ritual of taking [the bride], one should perform the ten-fold fire-rite.
The Name of Agni: Oṃ, svāhā to the fire born from the ocean. Meditation on Agni. Sixteen oblations of fuel-sticks (samidh).

The eastern libation (pūrvāghāra) and the northern libation (uttarāghāra). One should wrap the hand with the *upayamana* kuśa grass. Then, having performed the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*), the student (*vaṭu*) should be led [to his seat]. Having sat down on the northern part of the sacrificial throne (*yajñasiṃhāsana*), he should pay homage to the lineage of the Guru.
[Offerings for] Vaṭuka: [This is] for the worship of the Guru. This seat; flowers; water for the feet (pādārgha); water for the hands (hastārgha);

sandalwood paste; sacred thread and flowers; incense and lamp. For the purpose of the rite of Vaṭuka, one should prepare a mandala here before the form of the Guru measuring one cubit (hasta), using fragrant sandalwood paste.

Sprinkling: *Oṃ*. Filled upon the surface of the earth by the blood of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, I sprinkle [the ground] with fragrant water for the sake of removing its defects. Smearing the ground with the hand.
The earth itself has been purified, anointed with fragrant substances and water;
likewise, the sins committed in previous births—both misdeeds and good deeds—are cleansed.
In this life and in other lives as well,
[the self] is bound by the threads of karma, both in this birth and throughout successive births.
Having formed the añjali with the back of the hand, one should rotate it with the mind and offer it before the Guru,
who has arisen from the unbroken maṇḍala.
And flowers of various forms are born from various lineages;
may all that be forgiven, O Lord, and may you, Śiva, protect us at all times.
The maṇḍala for the purification of the latent impressions (*vāsanā*). [The deities are as follows:
Kevo, Voya, Piṃthva; Indra and the others; Dathoya and the others; Duṃthva, Sadyojāta and the others; and the three deities in the center.
He perceives; he flows; the one who has performed the sacrifice; that which belongs to the dog; that which belongs to the dog of the maṇḍala.

The worship for the purpose of departure: Oṃ, salutation to the Brahma-maṇḍala. Oṃ, salutation to the Viṣṇu-maṇḍala. Oṃ, salutation to the Rudra-maṇḍala. Oṃ, salutation to the Candra-maṇḍala. Salutation to the Agni-maṇḍala. Oṃ, salutation to the Guru-maṇḍala. Incense. Lamp. Hymn of praise (Stotra).
Homage to you, O Maṇḍala, and to you, the sovereign of all principles;
homage be to you, the Maṇḍala that illuminates the realms of Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ.
Here [are offered] perfume and so forth, as well as the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā). Having formed a handful of flowers, the student recites the mantra.
Oṃ! Grant me the authority for the practice of celibacy; show me your compassion.
O Lord, I shall indeed observe the ritual procedure and the command of my guru.
To this ignorant lump of flesh, grant me knowledge and devotion.
O Lord, please strive with all effort to destroy by your grace this body of mine, which is subject to transformation and born from a collection of sins.
My body has been purified by the Gāyatrī; may you increase my celibacy (*brahmacarya*). Grant me the vow spoken by Brahmā, as well as the bond and the study of the Vedas (*svādhyāya*).
By your command, I maintain moral conduct, purity, austerity, and knowledge.
Having recited thus and paid homage.
The dismissal of the maṇḍala. The Ācārya recites: *oṃ brahmacaryamāgāmu*. The Vaṭu recites:
*oṃ brahmacaryamāgāmi*. The Ācārya does not recite: *oṃ brahmacaryasānī*. The Vaṭu recites:
*oṃ brahmacaryasāni*. [He gives] the Vaṭu’s lineage [mantra], the *kuśa* grass, the unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), and the seat.
The Guru [performs] the sprinkling (*abhyukṣaṇa*) with the mantra: *oṃ āpo asmān mātaraḥ*. [He sprinkles] upon the head of the student (*vaṭu*);
[the meter is] the *gāyatrī*. May it protect.
The student, avoiding the wearing of lower garments, recites the mantra with the teacher.
Oṃ! With that immortal garment which Bṛhaspati wrapped around Indra, I wrap you, for the sake of long life, for longevity, for strength, and for power.
Thus is the binding with wool. For the binding with *muñja* grass, one should wrap it twice or thrice while reciting the mantra.

First Knot: Mantra: Oṃ! This goddess, the auspicious girdle (mekhalā), has come here, driving away misfortune and purifying my complexion. Bestowing strength through the out-breath and in-breath, may she, the beautiful and fortunate one, protect me. O [Name], of such-and-such lineage, I, whose name is such-and-such—Bho!

May I attain the state of celibacy (*brahmacarya*). The mantra for the second knot: *Oṃ iyam duriktam*. *Oṃ*, O Sarasvatī, guardian of Truth (*ṛta*) and of austerity (*tapas*), protect me; you are the victorious one, the motherless [sustainer]. [Name], of such-and-such lineage (*gotra*), and so forth. The mantra for the third knot: *Oṃ iyam duriktam*. *Oṃ*, may I partake of the equal and the unequal through these waters; I take hold of the protector of the sacred law (*ṛta*).
O Mekhalā, for Mārīṣa: [Name], belonging to such-and-such lineage (*gotra*), etc., one should recite with the Gāyatrī mantra:
*oṃ brahmaya-jñānam*, *oṃ viṣṇorarāṭ*, *oṃ namaḥ saṃbhavāya*.
The mantra for purifying the subtle impressions: Oṃ vaso pavitra. Perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) with the Jñānavijayā Gāyatrī mantra.
Having saluted the teacher with a verse.
Oṃ! This sacred thread is the supreme purifier, which was born together with Prajāpati in the beginning;
with that, I invest you for the sake of long life and Vedic splendor.
The dhāraṇī mantra of Vaṭuka.
Put on this foremost, auspicious life-prolonging sacred thread; may there be strength and splendor for you.
The mantra for the black antelope skin.
Oṃ! The eye of Mitra, the powerful splendor of Varuṇa—enjoy this fame and vigor.
I have uttered this speech; bestow upon me the prize-winning strength.
The mantra for the island of Laṅkā.
Oṃ! May Yaśas, Ādya, Pṛthivī, Yaśas, Drāya, Bṛhaspati, Bhaga, and Soma—may these all immediately attain glory for me.
The mantra for going.
Oṃ, clothed in new raiment, you have gone forth encircled; as soon as he is born, he becomes worthy of praise.
The wise poets, seeking the divine, impel him with their minds. [This is] the mantra for the yoga-path.
Oṃ, in every endeavor, [thee] most powerful. [Reciting] "ḍaṇḍakaṭhi kṛsnīnaviya," having taken up the staff of the student (vaṭu).
He recites the mantra: *Oṃ yo me daṇḍaḥ parāpatadvaihāya sodhi bhūmyām | tamahaṃ punarādada āyuṣe brahmaṇe brahmavarcasāya*. The mantra for the falling of the staff:
*Oṃ bhadro no agnirāhutiṃ bhadro rātiḥ śubhaga bhadro adhvaraṃ | bhadro...*

And for the sake of praise: The mantra for the bestowal of a seal-ring of gold and silver. The dawns are of golden form and free from conflict; both Indra and Varuṇa are delighted by the rising sun. Ascend, O Mitra and Varuṇa, to that sovereignty, to Aditi and Diti; you are Mitra, you are Varuṇa, you are Śiva.
What mantra has not been heard by me? *Oṃ gāva upāvanāvataṃ mahī yajñasya rapsudā ubhā karṇā hiraṇyayā*. O Khora, this is the mantra for dispersal: *Oṃ dīrghāyustvā*.

The mantra for sprinkling water: *Oṃ svasti na indro*. The mantra for the *kuśa* grass on the fingers: *Oṃ pavitrestho*. The preceptor shall offer water from the hand of the student (*vaṭu*). The student recites: "The water-bath.
*Oṃ āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvaḥ*. Second bath. *Oṃ yo vaḥ śivatamo rasaḥ*. Third bath. *Oṃ*.
Therefore, [the teacher] should cause [the student] to step forward; he should sprinkle water on the head of the *vaṭu*; the *ācārya* should offer a handful of water.

The student, looking at the sun, recites the mantras: *oṃ uru tyaṃ jātavedasam*, *oṃ citraṃ devānām*, and *oṃ tac cakṣur devahitam*. Having applied the *tilaka* on the student's forehead, [he applies] the clay from the Gaṅgā.
The mantra for the *cūlikā* is: *oṃ aśvakrānte rathakrānte*. The mantra for the *cetana-cetake* is: *oṃ*.

*Jadadyaka-vicitra*: The mantra for seizing the heart of the student. Oṃ. I place my vow within your heart; may your mind be in accordance with my mind. With one-pointed attention toward my word, may Bṛhaspati unite you to me. Then, the teacher [takes] the right hand of the religious student (*brahmacārī*).

Having taken hold [of him], he should ask: "What is your name? The *vaṭu* should give the reply: "I am named so-and-so, of such-and-such a lineage, sir. The *ācārya* recites the mantra: "Whose student (*brahmacārin*) are you? The *vaṭu* recites:
"Of you," [says] the teacher. "You are the student of Indra," [the teacher says]. The boy recites: "Of you."

By the teacher: "O Agni, you are the teacher. The student: "Of yours. By the teacher: "I am the teacher for you. The student: "Of yours. The teacher, having taken the student's right hand with his own right hand, should offer water with his left hand while the teacher recites the mantra: *oṃ*.
I entrust you to Prajāpati. I entrust you to the divine Savitṛ.

I entrust you to the waters and the plants. I entrust you to the two worlds, heaven and earth. I entrust you to the vastness of all the gods. I entrust you to the vastness of all living beings. Below, behind, and from the side, the teacher takes the student's hand.

Having taken [the vessel], having circumambulated the fire-pavilion clockwise, and having seated the student (vaṭu) on the right side of the teacher (ācārya), the teacher, facing east, should cover the student's right arm with two jars while holding them with his left hand. Then follows the worship of the deity Agni; then the worship of the deity Prajāpati.
Having mentally reflected, [he offers] the five oblations of *aruṇī*; having placed the residue, [he offers] the oblation of clarified butter.

Filling [the vessel] with oblations of clarified butter; having offered oblations of sesame seeds; the consecration of the *kalaśa* (vessel); the *saṃkṣāhuti* (purificatory oblation); the oblation: *Oṃ*, just as I shall speak this speech according to the ritual rules among the people—to the Brahmin and the Kṣatriya, to the Śūdra and the Ārya, to my own kin and to the stranger—may I be dear to the gods for the giving of the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*).
May my desire for rest be fulfilled; may the supreme one be propitiated; may he bow down; svāhā!
The Upanayana ceremony: Then the teacher should give instructions to the young students.

"You are a student of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārī*). The boy recites: "Yes. Again by the teacher: "Perform the *āposāna* rite. By the teacher: "One should perform the duties of a teacher (*ācāryakarma*). The boy recites: "Yes. By the teacher:
"Sleep, Mādirā! "Very well, young man! [said] the Teacher. "Restrain your speech! Place the fuel-stick!"
Be one who bathes daily; perform the worship at the three junctions of the day; perform the fire-sacrifice; and maintain the vow of a student.
Furthermore, the Master [stated]: "The avoidance of honey and meat; the avoidance of approaching those who should not be approached."
Service to the guru, the bearing of the staff, and the recitation of the Vedas.
One should observe the vow for as long as the month of Bhādrapada lasts. [This is] very firm, like a young student. Again, by the teacher.
In the presence of the guru, one must avoid wearing sandals or using an umbrella; one must not ascend to a higher place or speak in a loud voice.

Avarice and other such qualities are to be abandoned; sleeping on beds, sexual intercourse with women, and taking what is not given—these are to be avoided. *Vaṭu-vāḍham*. Then, having offered water to the student (*vaṭu*) with the *gāyatra* [sādhana] and the *praṇava* first, and having led [the breath] through the right nostril, [one should lead it back] through the left nostril.
The offering of the Revati verses. The offering of the Praṇava. Oṃ, the offering of the Gāyatrī.

Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, *tatsaviturvareṇyam*. This is the second bestowal of the Sāvitrī. Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, *bhargo devasya dhīmahi*. This is the third bestowal of Sarasvatī. Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, *dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt*. These are the Gāyatrīs.
Mantra for the oblation: *brahmajajñānam*. Oṃ *viṣṇorarāṭ*. Oṃ *namaḥ saṃbhavāya ca*.
Oblation. Gāyatrī: Oṃ *eṣa te gāyatro bhāgaḥ iti me somāya vratā*, *eṣa te traiṣṭubho bhāgaḥ iti me somāya vratā*, *eṣa te jāgato bhāgaḥ iti me somāya vratā*.
Vrūtācchaṃdo, by name, goes to sovereignty for me; for Soma, Vrūtādā, you belong to us; O Śukra, you are to be taken; having been chosen, you are chosen—svāhā! Pratiṣṭhā!
Oṃ, the impulse of the mind, the Gāyatrī, the offering. Then the student (vaṭu) should perform the ritual of the enemy of ignorance (ajñāri-karman).

Sprinkling water upon the fire, one should offer five pieces of wood: Oṃ agne suśravaḥ saṃsuśravaḥ saṃ mā kuru svāhā | Oṃ yathā tvam agne suśravaḥ suśravā asi svāhā | Oṃ evam ā gūṃ suśravaḥ sauśrava saṃ mo kuru svāhā | Oṃ yathā tvam... [as before] svāhā |
"You are the guardian of the treasure of the sacrifice of the gods; svāhā! Oṃ, in this same way, may I become the guardian of the treasure of the Veda for human beings;
guṃ svāhā! Having honored the fire and risen from it, he touches his ear and mutters this mantra.

With the *samidh* [verse]: Oṃ! Agni, fuel for the Great Star, for thee, Jātavedas, is the *bṛhat*. Just as you, O Agni, are kindled by fuel, even so may I be kindled with long life, with wisdom, with splendor, with progeny, with cattle, and with the luster of sacred knowledge (*brahmavarcasa*). May my son live; may my teacher [grant] wisdom.

May I be free from rivalry for three days; may I be possessed of glory, radiant, endowed with the luster of sacred knowledge (*brahmavarcasa*), and full of resonance—*gūṃ svāhā*. [Recite] this once, a second time, and likewise a third time. Again, having gratified the fire, one should again offer five pieces of wood with the mantra "O Agni, you of good fame" (*punar agne suśrava*). Again, having gratified the fire, one should offer oblations of clarified butter and oblations of sesame seeds.
He offers the oblation. Then the full [offering]. "O Brahman, to the Brāhmaṇa! "Oṃ, the first with the second! "To the end of existence!"

May the meanings of the mantras be realized. Oṃ saṃvaraṃ hiraṃtā guṃ. Now follows the libation of water (pāṇīya-tarpaṇa): Oṃ tanūpā agne asi. Now follows the rite for bestowing intelligence (medhā-karaṇa): Oṃ may the god Savitṛ bestow intelligence upon me;
may the goddess Sarasvatī bestow intelligence.

"O divine horses, bestow wisdom upon me; O Ashvins, grant me long life. Then, one should touch the limbs: "Oṃ, may my limbs swell with strength—speech, breath, sight, hearing, glory, and power. Then, one should apply the *bhasma-tilaka* (mark of sacred ash) with the mantra: "Oṃ, [the ash] which Jamadagni used for threefold longevity. Afterwards, [one should state] one's lineage (*gotra*).
One should recite the lineage name: "O Agni, originating from [the lineage of] such-and-such Śarman, I salute you."
To the chosen deities.
I pay homage to all the gods, the sages, and my gurus and ancestors. I pay homage to my fathers and mothers.
Oṃ, Agni is the sage; Agni is the blessing. Oṃ, through the vow one attains initiation; through initiation one attains the sacrificial fee;
the sacrificial fee attains faith; through faith truth is attained. The Self.

Blessing. The performance of the student’s alms-round (*vaṭubhikṣā*). [The student says: “May it be so; give me alms. [The teacher replies: “Oṃ, may there be well-being (*svasti*”). The mother should give the alms. [The alms] should be given by everyone in the world. [The student] should offer them to the Preceptor (*ācārya*). Now, the student is to be instructed regarding the remaining alms of the day and the consumption of food according to the rules (*niyama*). Then...
Sleeping on a bed with a frame for three nights, eating food that is neither pungent nor salty, and so forth— these are the various observances for awakening.

Until the month of Bhādrapada, the student (vaṭu) should remain strictly in silence. The student should carry out these words of the Guru. [Perform] the worship of Brahmins, rites for peace (śāntika) and prosperity (pauṣṭika), and the daily recitation. Oṃ pūrṇādarvvi. Then, when the sun has moved past the asterism, the student, having performed the evening twilight prayer (saṃdhyā), [should proceed] again.

The student (vaṭu) should perform the ritual acts for the teacher (ācārya) at the sacrifice according to the mantras as before. Then follow the rites for pacification (śāntika), nourishment (pauṣṭika), the remaining oblation (śeṣahoma), the barley and grains (yavadhānyādi), the formal dedication of food (annasaṃkalpa), and the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
The Full Oblation: Oṃ āpyāyasva same | Āsaṃsāra | The Offering of Bali | The Benediction.
Upon the conclusion of the sacrifice, the boy, having risen, should partake of alms and then give food to his mother.

[To the mother: "Give alms. *Oṃ svasti udakam* (Oṃ, well-being, water). Having placed [the vessel] on the ground, [one recites] the mantra for wrapping the bowl with water: *Oṃ ratyaṃ*, *Oṃ satya*, *Oṃ siṃcyaṃ*. The mantra for offering the five-fold first morsels (*pañcacāli*) is:
*Oṃ pṛthvi namaḥ*, *Oṃ pṛthvirājāya namaḥ*, *Oṃ prajāpataye namaḥ*.
Oṃ, obeisance to Agni. Oṃ, obeisance to Śrī. The offering of the *bali* to the spirits: Oṃ, svāhā to the Lord of Beings (*bhūpati*).

Oṃ, svāhā to the Lord of the World (*bhuvanapati*). Svāhā to the Lord of Spirits (*bhūtānāṃpati*). Oṃ, svāhā to the Lord of Ancestors (*pitṛpati*). Oṃ, svāhā to the Lord of Offerings (*balipati*). [He] recites the mantra over the vessel of food; [he recites] the *āpośāna* mantra.
Oṃ! He moves within all beings, in the secret cave, facing every direction.
You are your own sacrifice, you are the *vaṣaṭ* call; you are water, light, Soma, and immortality—*svāhā*!
The Mantra for the First Feeding of Solid Food (Annaprāśana): Oṃ, svāhā to Prāṇa! Oṃ, svāhā to Apāna! Oṃ, svāhā to Vyāna! Oṃ, svāhā to Udāna! Oṃ, svāhā to Samāna! Thus, the five morsels.
Again, the sipping of water: Oṃ amṛtopidhānam asi svāhā.
Then one should feed [the guests] as desired. Thus ends the procedure for the investiture of the sacred thread (*vratabandha*).
Then follows the procedure for commencing the Vedas.

One should perform the daily obligatory rites (*nityakarman*). Having performed the *ābhyudayika* rite for the occasion of beginning the Vedas (*vedārambha*), the teacher (*ācārya*) should perform the *kuśaṇḍikā* rite according to the rules and with the appropriate mantras. This includes the worship of the Brahma-vessel (*brahmākalaśa*).
At the conclusion of the Arthapadāsādhana: O Agni, the ten rites.
The names of the fires: *Samudbhavāgnaye svāhā*. At the end of the five *vāruṇa* [offerings], there is an oblation of clarified butter (*ghṛtāhuti*) for all;

an oblation of clarified butter for the full [offering]; and an oblation of sesame seeds (*tilāhuti*). Then, one should offer an oblation of sesame seeds for each of their respective mouths for all [the fires].
The consecration of the water-pot (*kalaśa-pratiṣṭhā*). The oblation for purification (*saṃskāra-huti*). Then, on the northern side of the sacrificial lion-throne (*yajña-siṃhāsana*).
The withdrawal from the student's vow, beginning with the downward breath (apāna) and so forth, [should be performed] according to the rules upon the surface of the Guru-maṇḍala.
The preceptor stands on the right side of the sacrificial throne, whether he belongs to both [the bridegroom and the father] or to this [the bridegroom] alone.
This rite is the entitlement for that meditation; thereafter follows the commencement of the Vedas. The student (vaṭu) faces the east.

The teacher, facing west, performs the initiation into the Vedas for the student (*vaṭu*). [He recites: "Oṃ, the *praṇava* and *gāyatrī*"; "Oṃ, fuel for the fire" (*samidham agnim*); "Oṃ, for the sake of food, thee" (*iṣe tvā*)—thus is the Vedic initiation. [Then follows] the oblation: "For the sake of food, thee" (*iṣe tvā*). The student shall perform the ritual of removing ignorance (*ajñāri-karman*) with mantras as previously prescribed.
Then Prajāpati, the creator of beings, should perform the oblation. This is the Brāhmaṇa-pūjā, consisting of rites for peace and prosperity.

The grains and other materials; the formal resolve regarding the food; the presentation of the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*); the recitation of the *Śaṃśrava* mantra; the removal of the purifiers (*pavitra*); the offering of the full vessel (*pūrṇāhuti*); the benediction (*āśīrvāda*); and the dismissal of the sacrifice (*yajñavisarjana*).

The Brahmā-earthen-jar consecration; the benediction; for the purpose of drawing the Brahmā-mandala; for the sake of the *yināya* (the lineage/teacher); for the sake of the Brahmā-earthen-jar; the feeding of the Brāhmaṇas; the consumption of the *vaṭula-vana* (wild fig forest) food.
Thus ends the procedure for commencing the Vedas.
Next is the ritual procedure for the Śrāvaṇī ceremony.

One should perform a ritual bath in the Vaṭu River. The *vaṭu* (novice) should daily perform the rites for the removal of ignorance (*ajñārikarma*). Then, the preceptor (*ācārya*), having prepared the materials for the sacrificial rite, shall offer the *sūryārgha* (water offering to the Sun) and perform the worship of the water-pot (*kalaśārccana*) for the sake of the *Śrāvaṇī-karman* and the rules of the vow, together with the *vaṭu*. Oṃ.

Regarding the passage beginning with *tattvājāma*: one should worship the seven sages (*ṛṣis*) at the front of the water-pot (*kalaśa*). Here, [one offers] perfumes and so forth. Then, one should satisfy the deities and others. Regarding the satisfaction of the sages: one should satisfy the young student (*vaṭu*) with a mixture of barley and unbroken rice (*akṣata*). Here, one should satisfy [him] with perfumes and so forth. If the father is not present, one should satisfy Kavyavāla and the others. Here, [one offers] perfumes and so forth.
The preceptor should perform the three rites with *kuśa* grass; the worship of the water-pot (*kalaśa*) should be performed according to the rule and the mantra.
The accomplishment of the word-meaning; the tenfold action of fire; the name of fire; the fire of emergence.
) Tra laṃṣanahāye || Svānataṃnake Brahmā Ādina || Stotra Yācake || Oṃ yaṃ brahmā caru || Mitaṃ phaṃ ṭāḍacā sagonanatvāye || Phaninicchāye || Oṃ trātāramindra ||

An oblation of ghee at the end of the five Varuṇas; an oblation of ghee for the Pūrṇā; an oblation of sesame seeds; the consecration of the water-pot (kalaśa); an oblation of purification (saṃskāra-huti); the two vows of the student (vaṭu-vrata); the lower garment and so forth according to the previous ritual procedure; the oblation with "Oṃ pavitrastho"; the noble oblation (āryā-huti); [the offering] to Vaṭuka, Kalaśa, Gaṇeśa, and Vajravairocana; then the eleven rites (ekādaśa-karma).

One should perform [the rites] as before: alms-gathering (*bhikṣācchuya*), the rite for wealth (*dhanāsiya*), worship of Brahmins (*brāhmaṇapūjā*), rites for peace and prosperity (*śāntikapauṣṭika*), barley, grain, and so forth, the formal declaration regarding food (*annasaṃkalpa*), the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), the final oblation (*pūrṇā*), and the concluding benediction (*āsaṃsā*).
Benediction; the final oblation; the ritual placement (nyāsa); the dismissal of the fire, the sages, and the offerings.

For the consecration of Koṭola-Ṣoḷaṃṣata by the seer Kuśa: Oṃ, for the sake of the seer’s splendor, I take you, the divine one, from Koṭola. Oṃ, go to the ocean, svāhā! [The seer] has led [the water] to the river.

The consecration with the water-pot (kalaśābhiṣeka); the benediction (āśīrvāda) beginning with sandalwood paste and other items; the bestowing of protection (rakṣāpradāna) upon the religious student (vaṭu); the dismissal (visarjana) of the goddess Komārī; then, the distribution of alms to the students (vaṭubhikṣā); the offering of parched grain (dhānā), fire-oblations (homa), and the providing of shade; having partaken of the meal (bhojya); and finally, the practice of eating only one meal a day (ekabhakta).
Thus ends the Śrāvaṇī rite.
Then follows the rite of returning home (samāvartana).

One should perform the daily obligatory rites (*nityakarman*). Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and the protection (*rakṣā*), and having performed the dismissal of the fire (*agnivisarjana*), one should place eight jars filled with water from sacred sites (*tīrtha*) to the east of the fire-pit (*agnikuṇḍa*).

Having performed the *ābhyudayika* rite for the purpose of the *samāvartana*, one should place the *thaṃka* and other items. One should perform the threefold ritual action (*trikarman*) using *kuśa* grass belonging to the preceptor (*ācārya*).
According to the prescribed rite and mantra: Brahmā-pūjā. *Oṃ tat tvā jām* and so forth. *Namaḥ to the lotus seat.*
Salutation to the sinew of the swan. Oṃ, salutation to Brahmā; [meditation].
[He saw] the plump, yellow, four-armed Brahmā with four faces.
And Daṇḍākṣa, shining with a swan-vehicle, holds a staff and a water-pot.

Salutations to Brahmā. Salutations to Prajāpati. Salutations to the Four-faced One. Salutations to the Creator of the Universe. Oṃ *brahmayajñānam*. Oṃ *brahmaṇaspate*. Oṃ *ābrahman*. Oṃ *dhāmacchad agni*. Here [are offered] fragrance and other articles. Worship of the eight jars. Salutations to Dharā. Oṃ *juṃ jate*. Salutations to Dhurā. Oṃ...
Idam Viṣṇu. Homage to Soma. Oṃ Irāvatī. Homage to the Waters. Oṃ Devaśruta.
Salutation to Anila. Oṃ dhiṣṇārṇukam. Salutation to Anala. Oṃ divo vā viṣṇu.

Salutation to Pratyuṣa. Oṃ, Vrataviṣṇu. Salutation to Prabhāsa. Oṃ, *viṣṇorarāṭam asi*. Here [offer] perfumes and other items. Oṃ, *ākṛṣṇena* etc. Oṃ, *trātāram indram*. Oṃ, *aśvastha* etc. Oṃ, *ardhamāsā* etc. External worship of the Gaṇas. Oṃ, *manojūtiḥ pratiṣṭhā*. Recitation (*japa*). Hymn (*stotra*). Oṃ.
"Above, in the Brahmāṇḍa, [the word] 'khaṇḍa' and so forth" refers to the end of the placement of the words. This is the ritual action of the ten fires.
The name of Agni: Oṃ, svāhā to Sūryāgni! An oblation of ghee; a full oblation of ghee; an oblation of sesame seeds.
The consecration of the jar (*kalaśa-pratiṣṭhā*). The purificatory oblation (*saṃskāra-huti*). One should bring the student (*vaṭu*) forward. Then, having drawn a mandala in front of the Guru.
Having formed the añjali with his hands, the student (vaṭu) should recite.
Oṃ! The vow of celibacy is the most excellent, the supreme vow among all vows.
For twelve years, this vow of yours has been broken by me.
May my body attain an increase in wisdom; may [he] grant me his blessing.
O Omniscient One, by the power of your vow, grant me liberation from my vows.
"May it be well," is the reply. The student recites:
"I shall initiate [the student]. "By the teacher. "Bathe. Then the student (vaṭu), having been instructed, should perform the ritual action.

The mantra is as before. Then, the two Ācāryas, having sat upon a seat of *kuśa* grass in the form of a *svastika* to the north of the fire, and having covered the *vaṭu* with a cloth and performed the *nṛvaṃcana* rite, the Ācārya takes small amounts of water from the eight jars into a copper vessel while reciting the mantra: *oṃ ye...*
The fires have entered within the waters. In the first: *Oṃ gohya*. In the second: *Oṃ upagohya*. In the third: [Oṃ].
Oṃ mayūṣā, in the fourth; Oṃ manohā, in the fifth; Skhalu, in the sixth; Oṃ viruja, in the seventh.

Oṃ tanūduṣu. [This is] the eighth. Oṃ indriyahāsi. One should cast the ocean [offering] as before with the mantra: Oṃ tāṃ vijahāmi. Thus is the offering of water (argha) and the ritual bath (arghasnāna). Again, with that same water, one sprinkles the boy inside the leaf-cup with the mantra: Oṃ yorocanāstava gṛhnāmi. Having placed it in a copper vessel.
The Consecration Mantra (Abhiṣecana-mantra): Oṃ!

With that [power], I consecrate you for glory, for splendor, for Vedic luster, for strength, for the faculty of Indra, for heroism, for the enjoyment of food, for wealth, for nourishment, for vigor, for honor, and with that by which the Asuras were scorched and the virtuous were established.
With that by which he consecrates the Soma, with that by which the earth was made great—that name the Aśvins bestow upon me as they consecrate me. The mantra for sprinkling again:
Oṃ, I take [the waters] from the luminous realms. Oṃ, with that very [power], I consecrate you for prosperity, for glory, and for sacred knowledge (brahman).
For the sake of spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*). The mantra for sprinkling again: *oṃ yorocanāstava gṛhnāmi*.
Oṃ! That [power] by which they made prosperity for me, by which they wiped away the sin, by which they sprinkled the two eyes, or whatever auspiciousness belongs to the Aśvins—[may that come to me].
Again, the sprinkling mantra: "I take that which is your bright essence. Oṃ āpo hiṣṭhā.
Again, the mantra for sprinkling: *oṃ yo rocanāstava gṛhṇāmi*. *oṃ yo vaḥ śivataḥ*.
Again, the mantra for sprinkling: *oṃ yo rocanāstava gṛhṇāmi*. *oṃ tasmā araṃga*. Again, the mantra for sprinkling: *oṃ yo rocanāstava gṛhṇāmi*. Sprinkling silently.

Again: *Oṃ yo rocanāstava gṛhṇāmi*. [The teacher] silently sprinkles water on the boy (*vaṭu*). Afterwards, the boy [is sprinkled]. With the mantra for the head-ornament (*mañjakoṭa*) and the bronze vessel (*kāsya*), [he recites]: *Oṃ uduttama iti*.
He causes him to tie the muñja grass around the staff; having placed it before the staff, he prepares a seat of black antelope skin.
Having placed [the vessel] silently, [he should do so] except for the putting on of the garment; the student (vaṭu), having sipped water (ācamya).

Facing the sun with hands joined in *añjali*, one should pour water while reciting the mantra: *Oṃ udyann bhrājabhṛṣṇur indro marudbhir asthāt prataryāvabhir asthāt daśasany asi daśasanim mā kuru vīdam mā gamayaḥ.* (First time) Again: Pouring another *añjali* of water...
One should cast [the water]. *Oṃ*, rising, shining, Indra has stood with the Maruts; he has stood with those who travel by day.
May he, the winner of hundreds, the winner of thousands, bring this wealth to us.
Second: again, one should cast a handful of water. *Oṃ*, rising, shining, Indra has stood with the Maruts in the evening.

"O you who stand with [the rays], you are the winner of a thousand; O maker of a thousand, having found us, lead us home. Having thus given the third [oblation] to Āditya, then follows the purification of the student's speech: "Call the student's mother," and having touched the student with the words of the astrologer.

Afterwards, having prepared warm water in a copper vessel at the sacrificial pit (*yajñakuṇḍa*), one should pour curd, white sesame seeds, and that [water] into it. Then, one should wash away the impurities of the hair with that warm water. Afterward, one should have the hair and nails clipped by a barber. One should perform the ritual bath. For the mantra for brushing the teeth with *udumbara* wood: Oṃ.
Arrange yourselves for the sake of food; let King Soma not come near you.
He who wipes his face is cleansed with glory and with fortune.

The sipping of water (ācamana). Then, the application of fragrant substances is performed silently. Then, the bath with the water from the eight jars is performed as before, with the mantra. This is the procedure for the bath. The student (vaṭu) performs the sipping of water. The mantra for the presentation of the sacred thread (yajñopavīta) to the student: "Oṃ yajñopavītam. The student performs the midday twilight devotion (madhyāhna-saṃdhyā).

The student stands to the north of the teacher. Taking sandalwood paste in his hand, he applies it to his mouth, nose, eyes, and ears with the following mantra: *Oṃ prāṇaṃ prāṇau me tarpaya tac cakṣur me tarpaya śrotraṃ me tarpaya*. [This is done] when the father is not present.

One should offer water with sesame seeds (tilodaka) to the ancestors. If the father is living, one says: "O fathers, be satisfied. Having washed his hands and taken sandalwood paste from the hand of the student (vaṭu), he recites the mantra.
Oṃ, may I be one with good vision through my two eyes; may I be one with good hearing through my two ears. Now follows the mantra for putting on new clothes:
Oṃ! I shall put this on; I shall prosper. For long life and for invincibility, I am this garment. May I live a hundred autumns, full of vigor; may I clothe myself in nourishment and prosperity.

Now, the mantra for taking the upper garment: *oṃ yasasāmādyā vā pṛthivī*. The mantra for wrapping the head: *oṃ yuvāsuvāsā*. The mantra for the heart: *oṃ jadadyaka*. The mantra for the dog: *ṭvāka svāna*.
Oṃ! That which Jamadagni [offered] as food for faith, for desire, and for the sense-faculty.
I accept them with glory and with fortune.

Wrap [the head] with garland flowers while reciting the mantra: Oṃ, as Indra made the celestial nymphs (apsarases) vast and wide, so, with that [same power], I bind this well-strung garland upon my head for the sake of glory.
Now, the mantra for the ear-ornament: *Oṃ, you are an ornament; may you be an ornament;
may I become [an ornament].* The mantra for applying collyrium to the eyes:
*Oṃ, you are the pupil of the rolling eye; you are the giver of sight; grant me sight.*
Give [it]. Then, the mantra for looking at oneself in a mirror: *oṃ rociṣṇur asi*.
*oṃ yūṃ jaṃti vr̥dhnam aruṣaṃ carantaṃ paritaṣṭhuṣaḥ | rocaṃte rodasī divi*.

The mantra for taking the umbrella: *Oṃ bṛhaspatecchadirasi pāṣmano romaṃ tardhehi | tejaso jasaśomāmantardhyehi*. The mantra for taking the two sandals: *Oṃ pratiṣṭhe stho viśvatomāpātam*. [With this,] one should place them on the feet. The mantra for the gift of a water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*): *Oṃ...*

May there be well-being for us; may Indra [protect us]. The mantra for holding the Veda-staff (*vaidadaṇḍa*): *Oṃ, protect us from all sides against all diseases and demonic forces.* One who performs the study of the Vedas and so forth, the cleaning of the teeth, and the ritual bathing, does not become a non-celibate student (*abrahmacārī*).

*Saṃbalaviya*. Oṃ, may you have long life! Then the mother spoke these words: "He has gone to another country. She was informed by his father, relatives, and friends; they brought the young student back. He arrived at the doors of the houses.
Having performed the worldly formalities as befits a man, the preceptor sits upon the sacrificial throne in the northern direction.
The oblation: *oṃ ākṛṣṇena*. The return ceremony: *oṃ manojyoti*.
Consecration; Brahmin worship; rites for peace and prosperity; barley, grain, and so forth.

The resolution regarding the food; the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā); the full oblation (pūrṇāhuti); the benediction for the sake of worldly prosperity; and the dismissal of the sacrifice (yajñavisarjana).
The dismissal of the bali offering; the consecration of the kalaśa; sandalwood paste; vermilion; the thread with its qualities (saguṇa); the benediction;
here, one should give the thread with its qualities to the local people and the brahmacārins.
Thus ends the ritual procedure for the Samāvartana ceremony.

Then, on the fourth day [of the rite], the boy did not see the sun. When the fourth day was complete, the boy saw the sun. While the sun was still present, the boy begged for *argha* with joined palms. He covered the boy with a garment. Having offered *argha* to the sun, the boy recited the mantra: "Oṃ, you are self-born, the most excellent..."
"Thou art the ray, the giver of splendor. Grant me splendor; I turn according to the turning of the Sun. [This is] the *sūryadarśana* (beholding of the Sun).

Having performed the twilight worship (*saṃdhyā*) following the student's ritual bath (*vaṭusnāna*) and other rites, having performed the propitiation of the animal-offering to Vināyaka (*vināyakapaśutarpaṇa*), and having performed the worship of the House-Kumārī (*gṛhakomārīpūjā*) with the preceptor (*guru*) and teacher (*ācārya*), [he receives] the blessing (*āśīrvāda*) from the student, sandalwood paste, and so forth. [This is] the Kumārī [rite].
The dismissal. The ritual agreement. The rinsing of the mouth with the remains.
Thus ends the fourfold procedure for the *samāvartana* (the student's return home).
Then follows the rite of marriage.

Svāhā! This for Candramas. To Brahmā, svāhā! This for Brahmā, and so forth. Bhūḥ, svāhā! This for Bhūḥ. Bhuvaḥ, svāhā! This for Bhuvaḥ.
