Svāhā! This [is for] the plants, the Apsarases, and the mushrooms. Oṃ, he who is well-disposed (sa-gūṃ-hita), the All-Soma, Sūrya the Gandharva—may he protect this Brahman and Kṣatra. To him, Svāhā! Vāṭ! This [is for] Sa-gūṃ-hita, Viśvasāman, Sūrya the Gandharva. Oṃ, he who is well-disposed, Viśvasāman...
Sūrya is the Gandharva; his Apsarases are the Marīcis, named Āyuvānās; to them, Svāhā!

This [is offered] to the Marīcis, the Apsarases, and the Āyus. Oṃ! Suṣumna, the Gandharva who is the sun’s ray and the moon—may he protect this Brahman and Kṣatra. To him, Svāhā! Vāṭ! This [is offered] to Suṣumna, the sun’s ray, the moon, and the Gandharva. Oṃ! Suṣumna...
Sūryaraśmi is the Gandharva, the moon is his portion; the Apsarases named Abhikṣurayas belong to him. Svāhā!
To these constellations, to the Apsarases, and to the Abhikṣurayas. Oṃ! Iṣira Viśvavyacās Vāta is the Gandharva; he is [the protector].

May this protect the field of Brahmā; to him, svāhā! Vāṭ! This [is for] the Gandharva named Iṣira, who dwells in all beings; and to his Apsarases named Ūrjas, svāhā! This [is for] the waters, the Apsarases named Ūrvas. Oṃ, Tujyu Suparṇa is the Gandharva of the sacrifice.
May this protect the Brahman and the Kṣatra; to him, Svāhā! Vāta! This [is for] Tujyu, Suparṇa, Yajña, and Gandharva.

Oṃ! The swift, well-winged sacrifice is the Gandharva; his Apsarases are the sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇās). To them, the Tāvānīs, Svāhā! This [is for] the Apsarases, the Tāvānīs, who are the sacrificial fees. Oṃ! Prajāpati Viśvakarman, the mind, is the Gandharva; he is...
May this protect the Brahminhood and the Kshatriyahood; to him, Svāhā! Vāṭ! This [is for] Prajāpati Viśvakarman, for Manas, and for Gandharva. Oṃ!
Prajāpati is Viśvakarman, Manas is Gandharva; his Apsarases are the Ṛks and Sāmans.
Svāhā to these Apsarases named Eṣṭis; this [offering] is for the Apsarases named Ṛkśāmas and Eṣṭis.

And mind, svāhā! This for Mind. And thought, svāhā! This for Thought. Oṃ, and intention, svāhā! This for Intention. Oṃ, and form, svāhā! This for Form. Oṃ, and the cognized, svāhā! This for the Cognized. Oṃ, and cognition, svāhā! This for Cognition. Oṃ, and mind, [svāhā! This for Mind.

Svāhā! This for Manas. Oṃ, and Śakvarī, svāhā! This for the Śakvarīs. Oṃ, and Darśa, svāhā! This for Darśa. Oṃ, Paurṇamāsa, [svāhā! This for Paurṇamāsa. Oṃ, and Bṛhat, svāhā! This for Bṛhat. Oṃ, and Rathantara, svāhā! This for Rathantara.
Oṃ. Prajāpati bestowed the victories upon Indra, the bull-like conqueror of Vṛtra;
for him all the people bowed down in the battles. He became the fierce one, he became the one to be invoked here. Svāhā!
This [offering] is for Prajāpati, for the victories, for Indra.

Oṃ! Agni is the lord of beings; may he protect me in this sacred word (*brahman*), in this field, in this blessing, in this office of priest, in this rite, and in this invocation of the gods—*gaṃ svāhā*.
This for the Lord of those who have become fire.
Oṃ, Indra is the lord of the eldest. This [is offered] to Indra, the lord of the eldest.
Oṃ! Yama is the lord of the earth. This [is offered] to Yama, the lord of the earth. Here, Oṃ! Vāyu is the lord of the atmosphere. This [is offered] to Vāyu, the lord of the atmosphere.
Oṃ, Sūrya is the lord of the day.
This is for Sūrya, the lord of the day. Oṃ! Caṃdramas is the lord of the constellations. This is for Caṃdramas, the lord of the constellations.
Oṃ! Bṛhaspati is the lord of Brahmā. This [is offered] to Bṛhaspati, the lord of Brahmā.
Oṃ! Mitra is the lord of truths. This [is offered] to Mitra, the lord of truths.
Oṃ, Varuṇa is the lord of the out-breaths. This [is for] Varuṇa, the lord of the out-breaths.
Oṃ, Samudra is the lord of rivers. This [offering] is for Samudra, the lord of streams.
Oṃ, Lord of the sovereign power over food! This [is for] the food, the Lord of the sovereign power over foods!
Oṃ! Soma is the lord of plants. This [is offered] to Soma, the lord of plants.
Oṃ! Savitṛ is the overlord of all instigations. This [offering] is for Savitṛ, the overlord of all instigations.
Oṃ! Rudra is the lord of cattle. This [is offered] to Rudra, the lord of cattle.
In this case, there is the touching of water for the purpose of consigning [the ritual items].
Oṃ! Tvaṣṭṛ is the lord of forms. This is for Tvaṣṭṛ, the lord of forms.
Oṃ, Viṣṇu is the lord of the mountains. This [is offered] to Viṣṇu, the lord of the mountains.
Oṃ, Maruta, lord of the hosts.
This [is for] the sovereign of the hosts of Maruts.

Oṃ! To the father, grandfather, great-grandfather, and those beyond them—the three ancestors—may this [oblation] reach you. In this sacred word (brahman), in this constellation, in this month, in this assembly, in this rite, in this invocation of the gods, may it be well; svāhā! This is for the fathers, for the grandfathers.
To the paternal great-grandfathers, higher and lower, who have attained the state of the gods; the lineage of renunciation; the ritual rinsing with water from the *argha* vessel.

Oṃ! May Agni, the first among the deities, release her offspring from the grasp of death. May King Varuṇa here grant his approval, so that this woman may not suffer the sin of losing a grandson, svāhā!
This is for Agni. Oṃ! May Agni Gārhapatya protect this woman; may he grant her offspring long life.
May she have a husband who does not fail her, may she live to see her son and grandson, and may she experience the joy of her kin.
Gūṃ Svāhā! This is for Agni. Oṃ! O Agni, worthy of sacrifice, bestow upon us all blessings from heaven and earth.
Whatever great wealth has been lost in this vast heaven, bestow that wonderful treasure upon us;
*gūṃ svāhā*. This is for Agni.
Oṃ! May the path be auspicious for us; show us the way and come to us. Grant us life that is full of light and free from decay.

May death depart; may I attain immortality. May Vaivasvata grant us fearlessness. Svāhā! This is for Mṛtyu Vaivasvata. [The deity] Yama, who is present here, is pleased. May the god [Yama] be satisfied.

Oṃ! O Death, go along the other path, that which is different from the path of the gods. I speak this to you who have eyes and ears: do not harm these offspring nor our heroes. Svāhā! This [offering] is for Mṛtyu Vaivata. [This is] the renunciation of the dwelling. [Perform] the sipping of water with the water from the arghya vessel. [This is] the *śaṃśrava* at the consecrated fire.
Having placed [it].
The oblation of clarified butter is filled with the oblation of all-clarified-butter.
Oṃ saptate agne. For the offering of sesame seeds, for all [purposes], for the consecration of the water-pot (kalaśa), and for the purificatory oblation (saṃskāra-huti).

The Lājā-homa: Fuel-sticks, ghee, parched grain, and clarified butter are offered. *Oṃ*. Aryaman, the god, has sacrificed for the maiden before Agni; may that Aryaman, the god, release her from death and from misfortune, *svāhā*. This is for Agni. Thus the first [offering].
Oṃ! This noble woman, scattering parched grain mixed with oil upon her knees, prays:
"May my husband be long-lived; may my kinsmen be free from disease. Svāhā!"
This is for Agni. I pour these parched grains (lājās) into the fire as a means of bringing you prosperity; may Agni grant his approval to this auspicious union between me and you. *iṣe svāhā*.
This is for Agni. Then the bridegroom takes the right hand of the maiden, including the thumb. [The Mantra:]

Then, at the time of the circumambulation of the fire, [he recites]: "Oṃ, may the gods take your hand for the sake of good fortune, that you may reach old age with me as your husband; Bhaga, Aryaman, Savitṛ, and Purandhi have given you to me for the state of a householder."
I am non-delusion, you are essence; you are essence, I am non-delusion. I am the Sāman, you are the Ṛc; I am heaven, you are the earth.
For we two are the two who marry one another; let us together deposit the seed.
"Procreating offspring, let us two bring forth; may we obtain sons. May our teeth grow old together;
may we, as a loving couple, radiant and of good mind, behold a hundred autumns.
May we live for a hundred autumns; may we hear for a hundred autumns. Then, standing on the northern side, [he says]: "Ascend this stone, Om."
Be firm for us, be with us;
overcome those who attack, and strike down those who seek to harm us. Ascend, O Mantra!
Now the Gāyatrī: Oṃ! Sarasvatī, come forward with this favor; O blessed one, rich in sacrificial food!
You who are at the forefront of the procreation of every living being, in whom all that has been and this entire world came into existence.
Today I shall sing that verse which proclaims the supreme glory of women.
Then they circumambulate the fire. [The groom] with his wife, and [the bride's father] with his daughter-in-law. "Oṃ, may he be auspicious by name.
"Oṃ, Agni, for you first did they lead away Sūryā along with her bridal procession; again, O Agni, give the wife back to her husbands together with offspring. [To the singers: "Oṃ, yours is Vāyu."

The son-in-law, having drawn the sun [with the plow], offers the parched grains (*lāja*) while performing three circumambulations clockwise. *Oṃ bhagāya svāhā*. *Oṃ prajāpataye svāhā*. [Accompanied by the ritual relinquishment (*tyāga*):]
[The bridegroom] leads the bride to the fire-pit within the shadow of seven steps: Oṃ, one step for food—may Viṣṇu lead you.
Two steps for strength—may Viṣṇu lead you. Oṃ, three steps for the attainment of wealth—may Viṣṇu lead you. Oṃ, four steps for well-being—may Viṣṇu lead you. Oṃ, five steps for livestock...
May Viṣṇu lead you. Om! To the six seasons, may Viṣṇu lead you. Om!
You have become one who has stepped seven steps; be devoted to me according to the Sāman; may Viṣṇu lead you.

The sprinkling with water-jars: *Oṃ āpaḥ śivāḥ śivatamāḥ śāntāḥ śāntatamāstāste kṛṇvatu bheṣajam* (May the waters, auspicious, most auspicious, peaceful, and most peaceful, provide healing for you). *Oṃ āpo hi ṣṭhā*. Beholding the sun: *Oṃ tat cakṣuḥ*. The mantra for the ocean: *Oṃ sindhurnāviye*. The mantra for the purifying cloth (*vasopavitra*): *Oṃ sindhu-cchāya*. *Oṃ*.

"Behold this bride, most auspicious; come together and gaze upon her. Having bestowed good fortune upon her, go back whence you came. [To the bridegroom: "O Sindhu, for the sake of joy! [The bridegroom: "Oṃ, Śrī is yours. [Touching the heart:
"Oṃ, I place my heart within your vow; let your mind be in accordance with mine; let your speech be one with mine."
O gentle-faced one, may Prajāpati unite you with me. Descend upon the ox-cart. Oṃ! Here the cows sit down;
here [the calves]; here the man; here the sacrifice with its thousand-fold dakṣiṇā; here may Pūṣan sit down.

The Vision of Dhruva || Oṃ, I behold Dhruva; I behold you as Dhruva. May Dhruva nourish me with prosperity. May Bṛhaspati bestow you upon me. Living with me as your husband, live for a hundred autumns, blessed with offspring. [Khvanomanapāne] || Ghee-oblation || Oṃ, svāhā to Prajāpati. Oṃ.
Sṛṣṭikṛte svāhā || Oblation of sesame seeds || Oṃ tryambakam || Vivāha || Oṃ mano jūtiḥ || Pratiṣṭhā ||
In the shade of the forest of debate.
Worship of the Brahmins; rites for peace and prosperity; parched grains of newly harvested rice; the formal consecration of food.
Worship of the directions; offering of oblations (bali-pūjā); the lamp of clarified butter; the presence of the sacrificial fire; the five Varuṇa mantras.

Protect [us], O Agni, Svāhā! Protect the sacrifice, O Radiant One, Svāhā! Protect everything, O Performer of the Rite, Svāhā! I offer this exceedingly red [oblation], Svāhā! Whatever is unknown or known, may that be for the sake of all; let it be [accomplished], Svāhā! All that, O Agni, you ordain when it is offered into the consumer of oblations, Svāhā!

To Vaiśvānara, svāhā! You are the expiation for the sin committed against the gods, svāhā! You are the expiation for the sin committed against human beings, svāhā! You are the expiation for the sin committed against the ancestors, svāhā! You are the expiation for the sin committed against oneself, svāhā!
You are the expiation for every sin, svāhā! And whatever sin I have committed...
The wise one has performed [it]. And that which was done by the ignorant—of that, you are the expiation; Svāhā! Oṃ, may there be well-being for us from Indra.
Oṃ, milk upon the earth. Oṃ, the imperial dominion of Viṣṇu. Oṃ, Agni is the deity. Oṃ, heaven is peace unto the end.
The sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) is given to the Brāhmaṇa. The offering of the *bali* oblations. The pouring out of the remnants (*saṃsrava*). Oṃ, may [the waters] be friendly.
The release of the strainers (pavitramocana). The full oblation (pūrṇāhuti). Oṃ devāgātuvi... Oṃ āpyāya... Oṃ hemasetvā...

Having performed the *āsana* (seating), the *āśīrvāda* (benediction). *Oṃ uttiṣṭha brahma*. The dismissal of Brahmā. *Oṃ viṣṇorarāṭ*. The dismissal of the *praṇītā* water. *Oṃ kastvā vimu*. *Oṃ apo adyānu*.
*Oṃ saṃvara hiraṃtā*. *Oṃ tanūpāgne asi*. *Oṃ yajñayajñaṃ gaccha*. Go, O gods.

The remaining oblations; one should offer betel nut; the ritual placement (nyāsa); the dismissal of the fire (agnivisarjana); the recitation, the touching of the head, and the consecration (abhiṣeka); sandalwood paste and other items, along with the bestowing of blessings (āśīrvāda); and finally, the meal together with the bridegroom. Thus, the rite of marriage is completed.
The festival born of wandering is Brahmā’s own extension; it is celebrated by the womenfolk at the crossroads. It is a festival of auspiciousness.
At the doors of the houses, having performed worldly customs such as bowing and so forth, [they enter] the pavilion of Lāsālāva.
Brahmāsa Svānatane. Sandalwood and other substances for the benediction. Oṃ Kāṇḍāt. Oṃ Mano Juti. Pratiṣṭhā. Hāsānagāyake. Vādāvanecchaya. Sephaṃ. Ārathi.
The Māsagheḍa; the Lāsālāva-thaṃtōyaṇa; the Sahabhojana-naka; and the Gvayaviyaka.
Thus ends the ritual for the Bhramanajātrā.
Then one should perform the fourth ritual act.

The daily rites consist of wearing a garland and applying sandalwood paste, eating together with the son-in-law (jāmātṛ), and performing the Kuśaṇḍikā rite according to the prescribed rules and mantras. This includes the worship of the water-pot (kalaśa) and the accomplishment of the meaningful words at the conclusion.
The *caru* ritual procedure; the tenfold fire-rite; the names of the fires: *Oṃ yojāgnaye svāhā*.
The eastern enclosure and the northern enclosure. Having placed the *saṃśrava* at the end of the western enclosure and the *prāsana* at the end [of the rite], [one should offer]:
*oṃ prajāpate svāhā*; *oṃ agnaye sṛṣṭikṛte svāhā*. One should place a water-vessel before the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) for the sake of the skull-bowl (*kapāla*).
This seat, obeisance. This flower, obeisance. Oṃ, svāhā to the skull! This [offering] to the skull.

The mantra for the oblation of clarified butter (*ghṛtāhuti*): *Oṃ agneḥ prāyaścittaṃ tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittirasi brāhmaṇastvā nāthakāma upadhāvāmi yāsyaipatighnī tanūstāmasyai nāśaya svāhā.* This is for Agni. *Oṃ vāyo prāyaścittaṃ tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittirasi...* ...you are the expiation of the gods.

O Brāhmaṇa, I approach you seeking protection; drive away from her that body which destroys offspring, and cause it to perish for her, svāhā! This is for Vāyu. Oṃ, Sūrya, you are the expiation among the gods;
O Brāhmaṇa, I approach you seeking protection; drive away from her that body which destroys cattle, and cause it to perish for her.

Svāhā! This is for Sūrya. Oṃ! Candra, you are the expiation; you are the expiation of the gods. I, a Brāhmaṇa seeking protection, approach you. Whatever in her is house-destroying, remove that from her. Svāhā! This is for Candra. Oṃ! Gandharva, you are the expiation; you are the expiation of the gods...
"You are the expiation; O Brāhmaṇa, I approach you for the fulfillment of my desire. Destroy her infamy, remove it from her—svāhā!
One should offer this ghee-oblation to the Gandharva. One should offer a full oblation of ghee and an oblation of sesame seeds.
The consecration of the jar (*kalaśa-pratiṣṭhā*); the oblation for purification (*saṃskāra-huti*); the bride; [the ritual] at the crossing of the Indus river.
Having sat upon a swastika seat on the northern side of the sacrificial throne,
facing east, [the officiant] should spread a human skin and place the *arghya* vessel before him.
Svānataṃnake || Metaṃphaṃ || Tāḍavo || Sagvana naṭvāya cusivarānajhuliṅole ||
One should purify [her] by means of the three [sacrificial fires]. During the installation of the fire in the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), one sprinkles the bride with water while reciting the mantra:

"Oṃ! You who were placed as a slayer of husband, a slayer of offspring, a slayer of cattle, a slayer of the home, a slayer of fame, and a slayer of the sons of your paramour—from this [state], I make you so that you may grow old together with me. Thus [ends the rite for] the auspicious [bride] named Amukadevī.

*Didhithem saṃpyāya*. The blessing with sandalwood paste and other items. The consumption of the *caru* offering. At the conclusion of the consumption, having sat upon the seat for the bride and groom, the oblation: *Oṃ śrīścate*.
Oṃ, may the mental radiance be established. This is the mantra for touching the heart of the bride.

Oṃ! That heart of yours, O fair-limbed one, which rests in the sun and in the moon—I know it; may we know it. May we see for a hundred autumns, may we live for a hundred autumns, and may we hear for a hundred autumns.
The Worship of Brahmins: Peaceful and Prosperous; for the purpose of the ritual, the sacrificial stream is offered to the deity.
Brahmālaṃkhaluye || Somādhe viya || Thus ends the procedure for the fourth rite.

In the year (?), on the waxing moon of Jyeṣṭha, on the eleventh lunar day (tithi), under the Aśvinī nakṣatra, in the Atigaṇḍa yoga, on Thursday, the ten rites (daśakarma) were completed according to the Brahmasūtra. This was written by the excellent twice-born Brāhmaṇa Śrī Jayantadeva. May there be auspiciousness for Sāṃphuliṃjura at all times.
Auspicious.
Oṃ! I draw forth the essence of the waters, the essence of the plants, the essence of the sun, and that which is well-composed.
Of the essence of the waters, of that essence, I take up the most excellent portion.
Oṃ! May my wealth and my dwelling, my ritual action and my power, my companion and my food, my movement and my goal be perfected through sacrifice.
With eyes on every side and a face on every side, with arms on every side and feet on every side,
the one God, generating heaven and earth, blows together with his two arms and wings.
Now, therefore, the daughter of the Sun, purified by austerity, wearing matted hair, bark garments, and skins—

She performed austerities while remaining concealed. For many thousands of years, she became renowned as Tapatī because she scorched [all] with her ascetic power and splendor. Chitraratha, the son of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, [said]: "O Brāhmaṇa, this girl, the daughter of the king, shall become your wife; she is not a widow, she has sons, her children are living, and she is a speaker of the highest truth."

One who speaks kindly, one who carries out errands, and one who speaks the truth—such a person abandons the Brahmin, the deity, the mother, and the father; he abandons his husband, whether he be unrespected, respected, or highly honored.
Just as Indrāṇī was to Indra, as Kauśalyā was to Daśaratha, as Sītā was to Rāma, as Mandodarī was to Rāvaṇa,
as Tārā was to Vāra, and as Añjanā was to Vāyu;
As Damayantī was to Nala, as Medayantī was to this [king] Eḍasā,
as Urvaśī was to Purūravas, as the Narmadā was to Puruṣa,
as Gaṅgā was to Śāntanu, and as Gāndhārī was to Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
Just as Kuntī was to Pāṇḍu, as Draupadī was to the Pāṇḍavas, as Śubhadrā was to Arjuna, as Herambā was to Bhīmasena,
as Bhānumatī was to Durjodhana, and as Chāyā was to the Sun; so too [was she].
Just as Rohiṇī belongs to the Moon, as Buddhimatī to Gaṇapati,
as Anasūyā to Tejas, as Lopāmudrā to Agastya, as Maitreyī to Yogeśvara, and as Sāvitrī to Brahmā; so [is she].
Just as Rukmiṇī belongs to Viṣṇu, and Umā to Paśupati, so may this excellent wife dwell in your home; may they all be well-pleased and remain well-pleased.
Now, therefore, follow the auspicious verses belonging to Indra, Varuṇa, and Soma—those that are most beautiful.
Oṃ! I take refuge in the Ṛgveda as speech; I take refuge in the Yajurveda as the mind; I take refuge in the Sāmaveda as breath; I take refuge in sight and hearing.
May speech, vigor, and power—vigor and the out-breath and in-breath—reside within me.
Whatever flaw there may be in my eye, in my heart, or in my mind, may Bṛhaspati mend that for me;
may he, the lord of the world, be our protector.
Bhūr bhuvaḥ! Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! We meditate upon that excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ; may he inspire our intellects.
With what aid has he become our wonderful, ever-increasing friend? With what most excellent protection?
Who among you, O truthful ones, has most gladdened us with exhilarations? Who, when drinking of the soma-juice, shall break open even the firmest wealth?
O Conqueror of the Worn-out Grass, protect us, your friends, with your aids.
With what aid do you gladden us, O Bull? With what [aid] do you bring wealth to our three [classes of] people?
Indra rules over the entire universe; may he be auspicious to us, both for our bipeds and for our quadrupeds.
May Mitra be favorable to us, may Varuṇa be favorable to us, may Aryaman be favorable to us;
may Indra and Bṛhaspati be favorable to us, and may Viṣṇu of the wide strides be favorable to us.
May the wind blow auspiciously; may the sun shine for our well-being;
may the god Parjanya, thundering, rain down for our prosperity.
May he bestow upon us prosperity by day; may he be established for us by night. May Indra and Agni unite us with their protections; may Indra and Varuṇa, to whom oblations are offered, unite us.
May Indra and Pūṣan grant us aid in the winning of booty; may the Soma-pressings be for Indra’s prosperity and well-being.
May the divine waters, having been pressed, be for our drinking; may they flow toward us with abundance.
O Earth, be pleasant for us, thornless, a place of rest; grant us wide space for our dwelling.
O Waters, you are indeed our life-sustaining essence; grant us strength so that we may behold great joy.
O Mother, like two longing wives, grant us a share of that most auspicious sap of yours.
Therefore, come hither; quicken us so that our seed may not perish; O Waters, give birth to us.

Heaven is peace, the atmosphere is peace, the earth is peace, the waters are peace, the herbs are peace, the trees are peace, all the gods are peace, the Brahman is peace, everything is peace; peace indeed is peace— be thou that peace, O Sāman!
May I not look upon this enemy with the eye of an enemy; may all beings look upon me with the eye of Mitra. With the eye of Mitra I look upon all beings;
with the eye of Mitra we look upon one another.
O seer, may I see for a long time; O one who speaks the truth, may I live for a long time; O one who sees the truth, may I live for a long time.
Homage to you, O Hara, to your heat; homage be to you, O Radiance! May your missiles pass us by; as a purifier, be gracious and auspicious unto us.
Salutations to you, O lightning; salutations to you, O thunder.
Salutations to you, O Blessed One; you strive for the light of heaven.
From whatever direction you intend [to act], grant us freedom from fear;
grant us security for our offspring and for our cattle.
May the waters and plants be friendly to us; may they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate.
May we see with that eye, granted by the gods, the bright light rising before us for a hundred autumns; may we live for a hundred autumns. May we hear for a hundred autumns;
may we speak forth for a hundred autumns. May we hear for a hundred autumns; may we speak forth for a hundred autumns.
May we be free from distress for many autumns, and may we be endowed with great prosperity for many autumns, and may we be secure for many autumns.
Oṃ! May you swell from every side with manly vigor, O Soma; may you be present at the gathering of strength.
May the strengthening powers swell thy head like steeds; may the virile forces that overcome the enemy swell thee.
Swelling for the sake of immortality, O Soma, place in heaven the highest glories as thine own.
Swell up, O most exhilarating Soma, with all thy purifying powers;
become for us most extensive, for our increase.
May the calf, impelled by thought, come from the highest dwelling place; O Agni, may it come to you with a song that yearns for you.
To you, O best of the Angirases, all the people dwelling in secure homes have individually offered their prayers with desire, O Agni.
Agni, desiring the dwelling-place of what has been and what is to be among beloved things, shines alone as the sovereign emperor.

Milk upon the earth, water. With the formula "Thee, by the impulse of the god," with the healing power of the Aśvins for splendor and the luster of sacred knowledge (*brahmavarcasa*), with those [powers] of Sarasvatī through her healing power for heroism and for eating, I sprinkle thee;
with the power of Indra for strength and for glory, I sprinkle thee.
May the waters purify me from mental impurity, as Drupada and others [purified] Vamumucāna, as one bathed from dirt, and as one cleanses with a strainer.
Rising above the darkness, we have ascended to the highest light—the god Sūrya among the gods—who shines far and wide. *Śrī* is yours, and *Lakṣmī* is yours.
Homage to Brahman; homage be to Agni; homage to the Earth; homage to the plants; homage to Speech; homage to the Lord of Speech; homage to the great Viṣṇu I offer.
Agni is the companion of Indra and the consumer of the oblations of the gods;
I shall accomplish what he intends to do, and I shall fulfill my vow according to his will.
O gods who dwell in the eleven-fold heaven, you who dwell in the eleven-fold earth, you who dwell in the waters by your greatness— you gods, may you graciously accept this sacrifice.

May the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus kindle you again; may the Brahmins and the Sun also do so through sacrifices. May you increase him with clarified butter, and may the desires of the sacrificer be fulfilled according to truth.

The Brāhmaṇa [reaches] up to Brahmā. The first [case-endings] with the second, the second with the third, the third with truth, truth with sacrifice, sacrifice with the *yajus* formulas, the *yajus* with the *sāmans*, the *sāmans* with the *ṛcs*,
the *ṛcs* with the *puronuvākyās*, the *puronuvākyās* with the *yājyās*, the *yājyās* with the *vaṣaṭ* calls, and the *vaṣaṭ* calls with the oblation.
May they crush each of my fears; Bhūr Svāhā!
Oṃ! We envelop you with the caul of the snow;
may the fire that has become a cool lake bestow healing medicine. Indeed, the fire that has become a cool lake shall bestow healing medicine.
Agni has brought near the one who is difficult to speak against; the hero has arrived.
And my heart is pained because of my son whose wings have not yet grown.
O Jātavedas, wander far for the sake of her who desires you.
Protect my mother and protect my sons; be a refuge for her.
O red-eyed one, O red-necked one, O black-colored one, homage be to you!

May Indra grant us sovereignty, and may you, O Varuṇa, grant us prosperity; let our enemies go to their destruction, and may we be victorious through the splendor of our sacred knowledge (*brahmatejas*). Just as the waves of the two oceans are filled with pearls, gold, and silver, so may Indra bestow dominion upon us.
May you, O Varuṇa, grant us abundance; let our adversaries meet their end, and may we triumph by the power of our spiritual luster.
Having established Kapila, Jatī, Sarvabhakṣī, and Agnipratyaṣya as deities,
and Varuṇa for your sacrifice, she protects my sons as long as the sun shines and as long as the moon glows.
As long as the winds blow, and as long as you live,
by whatever means one may live through delusion,
it is only through those acts of service that one truly lives; otherwise, one does not live at all.
By a single hand you are the earth, by a single city you are the world, and by a single umbrella you are the staff of my sovereignty.
Oṃ, homage to Brahman; homage!
The yogi of Brahman, whose eyes are his own vital breath,
is the essential nature of the gods; he is the eldest of all beings, lotus-eyed, seated upon a royal swan,
with limbs the color of a blooming champaka flower, possessing four excellent arms, and holding a rosary for recitation.
Carrying this eternal Veda and contemplating that entire host of sages, O best of the twice-born.
[I bow] to the glorious one who holds a lotus in his hand, the god of gods beloved by the best of deities,
the beautiful lord of heaven, who dwells upon the cool [summit], who brings auspiciousness to the world, who is the true seed and the life-force of all beings,
and who is [worshipped] by the wives of Yakṣas and Nāgas, by hosts of sages, and by all Siddhas and Vidyādharas.
I pay homage to Śakra, the guardian of the directions, who possesses a thousand eyes and whose body has the luster of a blooming lotus.
The world-protectors, Indra and the others, each residing in their own respective directions and joined with their own mudrās;
the planets beginning with the Sun always dwell upon this earth in their true forms;
the constellations, the yogas, the excellent holy sites, the Gaṇas, the Guru, the Vaṭukas, and the Mothers are present in the sacrificial altar or the water.
May Siddhi grant prosperity; may the earth be filled with sacrifice; may there be well-being.
Oṃ, salutations to Agni.
The eye of splendor, renowned as the universe, the source of existence, the purifier that removes the darkness of the sky, the sanctifier of the worlds Bhūr, Bhuvas, and Svar;
pervading all, saluted by the company of sages, radiant, with hands joined in devotion;
the inner self of every living being, the granter of desires, subtle, more subtle than the subtlest.
I bow to Ketu, the foremost among the planets, the teacher of all twice-born men, who has arisen with great splendor.

I bow to the perfected one (Siddhā), who is like the sacrificial fire that consumes the seven mountains and the self; she is filled with various desires and the arising of their fruits, bestowing the fulfillment of all wishes when the oblation is offered;
she is joined with the crest of vowels and consonants, and is praised by the accomplished ones.
O Śiva, you who bestow divine oblations, may you be our protector in the form of bliss.

May all those deities who are established in various arrangements within sacrifices— whether in the sacrificial pit, in the midst of the fire, or upon the mandala-altar together with their entire retinue—
be the gods who grant desired strength through mantras, satisfaction, and mudrās.
May the multitude of people, through the performance of the ritual of mudrā worship, exhaust the three defilements and reach the end of suffering.
The Rigveda is his first foot, the Yajurveda is his second foot, the Sāmaveda is his hand,
and this Atharvaveda is his second mouth— the utterance of the Vyāhṛtis and the chanting of the Veda.
May He whose body is the Gāyatrī, whose eye is the Upaniṣads, whose tusks are the Brahma-sūtras, whose covering is Viṣṇu, and who is the Earth herself in the form of the sacrificial Boar, be present.
May Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śakra, Jvara, Jamakara, Rakṣapāśī, Samīra, Jakṣa, Ānaka, and Durgā, together with the hosts of Grahas and all the Nāgas;
and Heraṃba, Siddhi, Saṃhā, and the goddesses presiding over the Moon and Sun— [protect us].
May all the gods, together with the foremost of deities, protect the Yoginī; may all the gods protect her!

All the gods, well-pleased and accompanied by the entire sacrificial offering, having consumed the oblation through the mouth of Agni, [bestowed] a full, auspicious, and entirely beneficial peace upon the son of Puṣṭi.
May they all, being satisfied, grant him his desired boons and bestow all perfections upon her.
O Goddess, O you who are the embodiment of sacrifice, salutations to you, whom all the hosts of gods worship with devotion.
May the deities of the directions residing in the water-pot and on the sacrificial mound be well-pleased; may they become bestowers of boons.
May the venerable fire-god Amuka-bhaṭṭāraka be well-pleased; may he become a bestower of boons.
May there be auspiciousness for the Brahmins.
May the king be victorious through righteousness; may the subjects be happy;
may all sentient beings be well; may the rain-clouds shower at the proper time;
and may there be peace and prosperity for bipeds and quadrupeds.

May the gods rain in due season; may the formidable earth produce an abundance of grain; may cows yield plenty of milk and other products; may the king, possessed of vast intellect, protect the world;
and may the noble daughter of a virtuous family destroy the faults of the people and the generations.
May this abundant devotion of those who possess devotion for the worlds prevail; may it be auspicious.
May there be the attainment of the sword-siddhi for the sovereign of Asmarāṣṭa.
May there be immovable success for the sacrificers.
For those accompanied by their hosts and retinues, may there be longevity, health, progeny, increase of wealth and prosperity, and the growth of their lineage.
May the virtuous be ever peaceful, their rise of sin destroyed;
may kings, established in righteousness, protect the earth at all times;
may the clouds rain in due season, and may the subjects be filled with joy.
May there always be joy, the increase of wealth, and delight in the company of kinsmen and friends.
May there be well-being for all subjects; may you, O lord of the earth, protect the world with justice. May there be perpetual auspiciousness for the Brahmins, and may all the worlds be happy.
May the rain-clouds pour forth in due season, and may the earth be rich with grain.
May this land be free from agitation, and may the Brahmins dwell without fear.

Whether performed through ignorance or non-ignorance, that which was left undone or done, and whatever was done yet deficient— may the mudrās, worship, ritual procedures, the sequence of sacrifice, the hymns, the ignorant and the wise, the faults in every sacrifice, and the oblation offered by Viriñci be [forgiven] by the sole Lord of all worlds.
With palms joined in reverence and with a serene mind, [he beheld] the blazing fire of all-perfect mantras.

O Sage, through my fault and the king’s, and due to fickleness born of devotion, I have caused suffering to you who possess such power. O Lord of the sacrifice, master of compassion, forgive this excess; O God, be the destroyer of my faults.
You are the refuge of all beings, encompassing both the moving and the unmoving;
having perceived the internal movement of all beings, O Supreme Lord, [you judge] them through action,
mind, and speech, and then through the administration of justice and other such deeds.
But in that city, O Consumer of Oblations, speech was unrefined and deficient.
O Supreme Lord, forgive that which is deficient in mantra, deficient in ritual action, likewise deficient in devotion, and deficient in recitation, fire-offerings, and worship.
May there be delight in Brahman.
The eighty distinct marks were preceded by the flesh of a quail;
when the months were complete, Māyā partook of that according to the prescribed rite.
Thus is the statement of Śaunaka: "By means of the ritual for the completion of the month, they [attain] longevity."
Vṛddhiśravas was born when Dakṣa performed the sacrifice; Vasu was born at the beginning of the Satya age;
Dhruva and Locana were born under the star Kanyā during the seasonal festival of Kālakānti.
The Pūṣan [hymns], the Vāmamānavas, the Viśve Devās, and the Daśātman [hymns] at the sacrifice.
Water, milk, dūrvā grass, curd, and jujube fruit—these should first be employed; the Vṛddhi-śrāddha is thus always prescribed.

Oṃ! To him of the Bhāradvāja lineage, [descendant] of Bhāradvāja and Aṅgiras, belonging to the Vānaspatya tri-pravara, of the Mādhyandina branch, of the Vājasaneyin-Caraṇa; to the one who is the sole supreme deity for the protection from saṃsāra, the thousand-formed one, the most excellent among those who grant supreme liberation, the great hero, the super-hero, the shatterer of the minds of the Daityas.
Śrī Śrī Śrī Gadādhara Parameśvara,
the sole expert in worshipping the lotus feet of the Sovereign of the fourteen worlds, the supreme Lord of gods,
the royal swan sporting in the lake-like heart of the Daughter of the Mountain King, the cherished deity, Śrī.

The lotus-like head of [this] most excellent among the twice-born is greyed by the pollen of the lotus-feet of the Calāneśvara Paramabhaṭṭāraka; he is one to whom the Goddess Śrīmatīśvarī— the beloved deity who bestows all people’s wealth, grain, jewels, livestock, and servants— has granted her grace through the boon she has received.

The unique great sun for the blossoming of the vast forest [of knowledge], the ornament of Dakṣiṇāpatha, who was uniquely skilled in the meanings of the Vedic scriptures such as the Paścimāmnāya, Śrīvaiṣṇava, Sāṃbhavīvidyā, the Vedas with their Pada and Krama recitations,
metrics, phonology, the Saṃhitās, Mīmāṃsā, and so forth; who was the illuminator of the Yajurveda, the Vedāṅgas, the Smṛtis, and the six ritual duties (ṣaṭkarman).
O Śrī Tilamādhava, the ornament uniquely skilled in protection, born from the lineage of Adbhuta; residing at Śrī Bhaktāpurī near the site of Sthānabhūmi,
I bow to you in the Himasthāna temple of the royal family, [offering this] to the great-grandson and grandson of Śrī Amukadeva Somaśarman.
For a son; for one desiring a daughter: I pay homage to the *gotras* of the royal family, the Brahmins, and the *cāraṇas*, svāhā!

Of the Kauśika lineage and Kauśika ancestry, with the three *pravara*s of Viśvāmitra, Devarāja, and Arundhatī-Kauśika, belonging to the Mādhyandina recension of the Vājasaneyi school; in the Brāhmaṇa family of Pradyotita, which is resplendent and devoted to the worship of the illustrious Garuḍa-Nārāyaṇa, there is this splendor.
Of him who shines forth pre-eminently; who has been pacified by the boon obtained from his chosen deity, Śrī Bhairava;

whose Brahmanic luster blazes intensely; who is white with the culmination of the knowledge of Brahman; who is intent upon the worship of Śrī Kānti Mahābhairava; and who is constantly engaged in sacrificing for himself and officiating at sacrifices for others.

One who is devoted to the six duties of studying, teaching, giving, and receiving; who has mastered the Rig, Yajur, Sāma, and Atharva Vedas along with their Pada and Krama recitations, as well as phonetics (śikṣā), ritual manuals (kalpa), grammar (vyākaraṇa), etymology (nirukti), astronomy (jyotiṣa), prosody (chandas), and the selection of hymns (viciti)—that is, one who has reached the further shore of the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences (vedāṅgas); and who is proficient in logic (nyāya), dialectics (tarka), and critical analysis (khaṇḍana).

Of the illustrious Amukadevaśarman, an expert in all the scriptures such as the Vaiśeṣika and others, a member of the lineage of supreme Vedic scholars from the land of Śrī Nepāla, and the sole thousand-rayed sun causing the lotus-like family of the twice-born to blossom.
The opening of the lineage of the Brāhmī [gotra] is the triple purification.
The hair-line [of the eyebrows] should be shaved three finger-breadths wide with the hair removed from the outside;
the staff should be seven cubits long, and the water-strainer (maṣala) should be likewise.
The yoga-cloth, staff, girdle, and *muñja* grass—these are the characteristics of the ascetic.

Of the lineage of Bhāradvāja, belonging to the triple *pravara* of Bhāradvāja, Āṅgirasa, and Vārhaspatya, a student of the Mādhyandina branch, a follower of the Vājasaneyi school, a practitioner of the *caraṇa*-meditation, born from the jewel-encircled realm of illustrious Nepal— of the venerable Śrī-Śrī-Garuḍanārāyaṇa.
To the venerable Goddess Jayavājeśvarī, who is solely intent upon the worship of the lotus feet [of her guru], who is a honey-bee to the nectar of the glorious lotus feet of Śrī Śrī Paśupati,
and whose head is purified by the pollen from the lotus feet of the venerable Mother Īśvarī Mātṛkā.

Of him who rejoices in worship, who is devoted to pleasing the feet of the illustrious Śrī Kanakacūḍākṣa Sadāśiva, who has been further strengthened by the grace obtained as a boon from his chosen deity, the illustrious Kubjikeśvarī,
and who is the sole illuminator of the lotus of his own lineage— the supreme among the noble lineages of the Śrī Pūrvāghāṭa Mahāpāñcālika.

[I am], the great-grandson of Śrī Amuka-pratyārādhya Somaśarman— who was an ornament to the lineage of the Brāhmaṇas of the Yajurveda and who was exalted by his proficiency in the investigation of various scriptures such as the Vedas, Vedāṅgas, Śruti, Smṛti, Itihāsa, Purāṇa, Āgama, and so forth; [I am] seeking a daughter for my son.

Oṃ! To the Brāhmaṇa named Tejaḥ, who belongs to the Kauśika lineage and the Kauśika clan, whose three *pravara* are Viśvāmitra, Devarāja, and Arundhatī-Kauśika, who follows the Mādhyandina recension and the Vājasaneyin-Charaṇa, and who is devoted to the worship of the glorious Garuḍa-Nārāyaṇa— śrī śrī śrī.

Of the illustrious Śrī-Śrī-Śrī-Bhaṅgiri—who shines forth preeminently; who has been pacified by the boon of his chosen deity; whose Brahmanic luster blazes intensely; who is white with the culmination of the knowledge of Brahman;
who is intent upon the worship of the glorious Kāntimahābhairava; and who is constantly engaged in sacrificing, officiating at sacrifices, studying, and teaching.
To one who is devoted to the six duties including the giving and receiving of gifts, who has mastered the Vedas— the Ṛg, Yajur, Sāma, and Atharva—

as well as the Vedāṅgas such as *pada*, *krama*, phonetics (*śikṣā*), ritual manuals (*kalpa*), grammar (*vyākaraṇa*), etymology (*nirukti*), astronomy (*jyotiṣa*), prosody (*chandas*), and metrics (*viciti*), and who is proficient in logic (*nyāya*), dialectics (*tarka*), refutation (*khaṇḍana*), Vaiśeṣika, and so forth.
Of one skilled in all the *śāstras*, a descendant of a lineage of supreme Vedic scholars from the illustrious country of Nepal,
a unique thousand-rayed sun causing the lotus-like family of the twice-born to blossom; [this is] the *Triprakvaccha* Brāhmaṇa clan,
with the *juroṃ* of the recitation of the lineage name.
Oṃ, homage to Vaiśvānara! The venerable Kātyāyana said:
I shall describe the mouth of the purifier (Agni), as it was spoken by the Lotus-born One for the benefit of the Brahmins and for the sake of the consecration of the fire.
Pāvaka, Bhāṇḍaka, Lokika, Dṛṣṭātmaka,
Kīṣṭorbhava, and Agni are proclaimed as his names.
The fire-god named Marut is prescribed for the rite of conception (garbhādhāna);
for the rite of male-ascertainment (puṃsavana), Candramas is auspicious for virtuous deeds.
Sīmanta is among auspicious rites; Pragarbha is for the birth-rite (jātakarman);
Pārthiva is for the naming ceremony (nāmakaraṇa); and Suciṣṭha is established for the sitting on the seat (prāsana).
In the *Cūḍākarṇa*, at the mention of the vows by the virtuous, one should recite the names beginning with "Origin" (*samudbhava*),
and at the conclusion of the vows, the fourth [name], "Sūrya."
In the gift of cows, the fire named Sūrya is prescribed; in marriage, the fire named Jaukasa is remembered; the fourth is named Śiṣi; and others say the fire is Dhṛti.
You are indeed named Āvasathya; Pāvaka is the Vaiśvadeva fire;
Brahmā is the Gārhapatya fire, and Īśvara is the Dakṣiṇāgni.
He is the bearer of oblations for the gods, the carrier of funeral offerings for the ancestors, and the expiation for errors in the *pākayajña* sacrifices; he is indeed the thousandfold power.
In Śrāvaṇa, Śravaṇāgni is in Agnicāndha;
in Pātāla, Dhanañjaya performs the sacrificial rite for Hotraka and Vadavānala.
In a *lakṣa*-homa, the fire is named Vahni; in a *koṭi*-homa, it is Hutāśana;
in the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*), it is Mṛdu; and in rites for pacification (*śāntika*), it is remembered as Tālaka.
For nourishment, there is the binding of strength; for the sake of fame, there shall be prosperity.
For the purpose of subjugation, it is named "Kāmada" (the Giver of Desire), which bestows the fruit of fulfillment.
In the Kaulika [rite], however, one should employ the Fire of Mars; in the case of the belly, it is known as Jathara;
for malevolent rites (abhicāra), the Fire of Wrath; and for the consumption of the dead, Kravyāda.
In the cremation ground, the fire of the hungry ghosts (preta) becomes the Samvartaka fire;
in the mantra, it is named Bhairava, and in the eyes, it is indeed the Rudra-fire.
In the ear, however, are Śivanāman and Vṛttinī; in the day and fire are Ādityā, named Kapilā; and likewise Soma and Maṅgala.
Aṅgāra and Dhūmaketu are for Budha;
Jaṭharāgni is for Devaguru; and Hāṭaka is traditionally taught as the [mantra] of Śukra.
Śani is named Tejognika, and Rāhu is indeed Hutāsana;
Ketu is named Rudrāgnika, and Rāhu is indeed Hutāsana.
The fire named Ketu-rudrāgnika is for prosperity in the rites of releasing a bull;
Vaiśvānara is the deity for the quarters; and one should worship Anala in the case of a young child. Gaṇeśvara and Gajāgni are for the auspicious occasion of the birth of a son.
The seven tongues of flame flicker within the mouth of that consumer of oblations;
he consumes the offering properly presented by the best of the twice-born.
Kālī, Kalālī, Manojava, Vasudharmmavarṇā, and Sthūlāṅginī—these have been forgotten;
Līlāyā and Nānā are the seven tongues of flame (saptajihvā), two for pacification (śāntika) and two for nourishment (puṣṭika), and Trisobhiyalīna likewise.
For if a wise man, not having found fire, should nevertheless perform a homa,
he would obtain neither the oblation, nor the consecration, nor indeed the fruit of the ritual action.
Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "Agni."
To the illustrious Sūrya: Oṃ ākṛṣṇena. To Paśupati: Oṃ yā te rudra.
Garuḍanārāyaṇa: Oṃ viṣṇorarāṭa. Śaṅkaranārāyaṇa: Oṃ idaṃ viṣṇu.
Jhaṃkeśvarī || Oṃ Bṛhaspate || Matteśvarī || Oṃ Ambe Ambi ||
Siddhilakṣmī. Oṃ śrīścate. Kubjikā. Oṃ dyāmmāle.
Varuṇa. Oṃ, obeisance to the serpents. [This is] the Upādhyāya’s ritual for the worship of Devajuroṃ.

It is beneficial, conducive to welfare, increasing prosperity, and indeed most auspicious; for it brings about many benefits and great increase. Its names are "Victorious" (*jaya*) and "Auspicious" (*kalyāṇa*); one should follow these names. You are the earth, you are the foundation, you are the support—therefore, one who sacrifices with the horse-sacrifice (*aśvamedha*) [attains this].
[The ritual] beginning with *sarva* proceeds for the month...

*Oṃ*, I milk [the cow] at will, O yielder of desires, for Mitra and for Varuṇa... [for] the subjects and the plants. Then, with the eastern half, the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) is given at will... for Varuṇa and [the others].
"O Indra, for the Aśvins, I purify [thee] for all creatures and for the plants"—thus, for all the deities, one has milked all desires. Oṃ Ā... vā... || Mātar, become [my mother]; give me alms.
Brāhmaṇa: O Mother, may you prosper; give me alms. Kṣatriya: May you prosper; give me alms.
O Vaiśya, there is no distinction regarding the fruit of alms.
Oṃ! By the Vasa-weapon and by the season, the divine Vasus, praised as threefold, have, with the Rathantara and with splendor, bestowed vital strength upon Indra at the beginning.
Oṃ! By means of the summer season, the gods, the Rudras, praised with the fifteenfold hymn, have bestowed strength upon Indra through the Bṛhat-sāman and the Ājya-śastra.
Oṃ! By means of the rains, the seasons, the Ādityas, and the seventeenfold hymn of praise, may we, through the form of Vai [Rūpa], attain the oblation for Indra.

Oṃ! By means of the essential season, the gods, being the thirty-three seasons, have established the splendor of the Vairāja hymns; they have placed this oblation, which possesses sensory power, within the Śrī.
By means of the winter season, O Maruts, you gods were praised by me; with the *śakvarī* metre as a boon, Indra and the gods established the *saha* oblation for as long as it shall endure.
Oṃ! By the season of Śiśira, the three gods have been praised by the Triguṇas;
with a hundred [oblations], they have established the wealthy, sovereign, and sensory-power-bestowing oblation.
The Veda [is the knower] of the six seasons, beginning with spring.
A wise man should have a seat made with one hundred and eight [blades of kuśa grass], half of that for the *viṣṭarāsana*,
half of that for the *upayamana*, half of that for the sword of knowledge (*jñānakhaḍgaka*),
and half of that for the fire-altar (*agnivedī*).
At the wedding, the *śuṅkarī* (the cooked offering) should be wrapped twice with yellow threads;
at the *garbhādhāna*, it is wrapped with a single thread; and at the *sīmantonnayana*, one should offer it together with the eight auspicious cakes (*aṣṭamaṅgalapūpa*) wrapped with three threads.
